g.L1.alphabet.title: Alphabet & pronunciation
g.L1.alphabet.reference:
Turkish has **29 letters** and is written the way it is spoken: every letter always has the same sound.

A B C Ç D E F G Ğ H I İ J K L M N O Ö P R S Ş T U Ü V Y Z

There is **no q, w or x**: *taksi* "taxi", *vize* "visa".

**Letters that trick English speakers**

| Letter | Sounds like | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **c** | English **j** in *jam* | *cami* "mosque" |
| **ç** | **ch** in *church* | *çay* "tea" |
| **ş** | **sh** in *ship* | *şu* "that" |
| **ı** (no dot) | the vowel in *ros**e**s*, said without rounding the lips | *kız* "girl" |
| **ö** | German **ö**: say *e* with rounded lips | *göz* "eye" |
| **ü** | German **ü**: say *i* with rounded lips | *gün* "day" |
| **ğ** | silent: it lengthens the vowel before it | *dağ* "daa", *yağmur* "yaamur" |

**ğ** never starts a word. After **e** or **i** it often sounds like a light *y*: *değil* ≈ "deyil".

**Dots matter.** *kır* "countryside" ≠ *kir* "dirt", *kız* "girl" ≠ *kaz* "goose", *öl* "die!" ≠ *ol* "be!", *kül* "ash" ≠ *kul* "servant".

**Capitals:** i ↔ **İ** and ı ↔ **I** are two different pairs: *İstanbul*, *Irmak*.

**Stress** usually falls on the **last** syllable: *ki**tap***, *ara**ba***. Exceptions (place names, some words such as ***mer**haba*) are marked as they come.

g.L10.loc.title: Locative -DA: in / at / on
g.L10.loc.reference:
**-DA** means *in*, *at* or *on*: **ev·de** "at home", **masa·da** "on the table", **çanta·da** "in the bag".

**Vowel (A):** look at the *last* vowel of the word.
a ı o u → **-da** · e i ö ü → **-de**

**Consonant (D):** after one of the voiceless consonants **f s t k ç ş h p** ("**F**ı**st**ı**kç**ı **Ş**a**h**a**p**") → **-ta / -te**; otherwise **-da / -de**.

The word itself never changes before -DA: *kitap → kitapta*, *mutfak → mutfakta*.
Exception: a compound like *yatak odası* adds **n**: *yatak odası·n·da* (explained in L24).
After a plural: **ev·ler·de** "in the houses".

First and last vowels differ in harmony: only the last one counts

g.L11.loc_copula.title: Location + 'to be'; apostrophes on names
g.L11.loc_copula.reference:
To say *I am at home*, put the "to be" endings from L5 **after** -DA:

| Pronoun | Form | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| ben | ev·de·**yim** | I am at home |
| sen | ev·de·**sin** | you are at home |
| o | ev·de | he / she is at home |
| biz | ev·de·**yiz** | we are at home |
| siz | ev·de·**siniz** | you (pl. / polite) are at home |
| onlar | ev·de(·**ler**) | they are at home |

**Buffer y:** -DA always ends in a vowel, so *-(y)Im* and *-(y)Iz* always get their **y**: ev·de·**y**im, park·ta·**y**ız.

**Harmony:** the person ending looks at the vowel of -DA. **-da** → -yım, -sın, -yız, -sınız, -lar · **-de** → -yim, -sin, -yiz, -siniz, -ler.

**Questions and negation** work as in L6–L7: *Evde misin?* "Are you at home?" · *Evde değilim.* "I'm not at home."

**Names take an apostrophe** before any ending: *İstanbul'da*, *Ankara'dayım*, *Ali'de* "Ali has it, it's with Ali". The ending follows the usual rules: *Ahmet'te* (t after t).

*Neredesin?* "Where are you?" = nere·de·sin.

g.L12.abl.title: Ablative -DAn: from
g.L12.abl.reference:
**-DAn** means *from*: **ev·den** "from home", **okul·dan** "from school", **İstanbul'dan** "from Istanbul".

It is the locative **-DA** plus **n**, so the same two questions decide its form:

- **Vowel (A):** last vowel a ı o u → **-dan** · e i ö ü → **-den**
- **Consonant (D):** after **f s t k ç ş h p** ("Fıstıkçı Şahap") → **-tan / -ten**; otherwise **-dan / -den**.

The word itself doesn't change: *kitap → kitaptan*, *sokak → sokaktan*. Exception: a compound like *yatak odası* adds **n**, as with -DA: *yatak odası·n·dan*. After a plural: **ev·ler·den**.

**With "to be" endings** (L11), no verb is needed: *Neredensin?* "Where are you from?" — *Londra'danım.* "I'm from London." -DAn ends in a consonant, so there is **no buffer y**: Londra'dan·**ım**, İzmir'den·**iz**.

*Nerelisin?* (the L5 phrase) is the more standard way to ask where someone is from; *Neredensin?* is fine in conversation.

⚠️ Don't mix them up: *Londra'dayım* "I'm **in** London" · *Londra'danım* "I'm **from** London".

Names keep their apostrophe: *Türkiye'den*, *Ahmet'ten*.

g.L13.clitic_de.title: Clitic de/da 'too' vs locative -DA; ve, ama
g.L13.clitic_de.reference:
**de / da** = *too, also*. It is a **separate word**, placed right after the word it adds to:

*Ben de.* "Me too." · *Ayşe de evde.* "Ayşe is at home **too**." · *Kitap da çantada.* "The book is in the bag **too**."

- **Vowel:** a/e harmony with the word before: a ı o u → **da**, e i ö ü → **de**.
- **Consonant:** it **never** becomes *te / ta*: *Ahmet **de***, *kitap **da***, *tavuk **da*** (not ~~Ahmet te~~, ~~kitap ta~~).

**Separate or attached?** The locative **-DA** is *attached* and does change d → t: *kitap**ta*** "in the book", *Ahmet'**te*** "with Ahmet". Test: leave the word out. If the sentence still makes sense, it was the clitic: *Ahmet ~~de~~ parkta* → *Ahmet parkta*. ✓

Both together: *Ev**de** **de** kedi var.* "There's a cat at home **too**."

The clitic never takes an apostrophe. Watch these pairs: *Ali de* "Ali too" / *Ali'de* "Ali has it, it's with Ali"; *ben de* "me too" / *bende* "with me, I have it".

**ve** = *and* joins words: *Ali ve Ayşe evde.*
**ama** = *but* joins two statements: *Ali evde ama Ayşe okulda.*

patterns.description: de after e i ö ü, da after a ı o u
The clitic never becomes te / ta (Ahmet de, kitap da)
Separate 'too' vs attached locative (Ahmet de / Ahmet'te)

g.L14.imperative.title: Verbs: infinitive -mAk, commands
g.L14.imperative.reference:
**Infinitive -mAk.** The dictionary form of every verb ends in **-mak** or **-mek** ("to …"), by a/e harmony with the stem: **gel·mek** "to come", **otur·mak** "to sit", **oku·mak** "to read".

**The stem = the informal command.** Take away -mAk and you have an order to one friend (*sen*): **Gel!** "Come!" · **Otur!** "Sit down!" · **Oku!** "Read!" · **Bak!** "Look!"

**Polite / plural command -(y)In, -(y)InIz.** To a stranger, an older person or several people:

| Stem ends in… | Ending | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| a consonant | **-In** (4-way harmony) | gel·**in**, otur·**un**, bak·**ın**, gör·**ün** |
| a vowel | **-yIn** (buffer y) | oku·**yun**, bekle·**yin** |

**-(y)InIz** is more formal still (signs, announcements, very polite speech): *Lütfen oturunuz.* "Please be seated."

**Stem changes before a vowel:**
- **git → gidin**, **et → edin**: t becomes d. Only these two (and a few rare verbs) do it: *yap → yapın*, *bak → bakın*, *iç → için* don't change.
- **ye → yiyin**, **de → deyin**.

**lütfen** "please" goes at the start or the end: *Lütfen oturun.* / *Oturun, lütfen.*

Polite command after a vowel: buffer y (okuyun, bekleyin)

g.L15.prog.title: Present continuous -(I)yor
g.L15.prog.reference:
**-(I)yor** + person ending = *I am …ing* **and** *I …* (habits, general present):
*Geliyorum.* "I'm coming." · *Her gün çay içiyorum.* "I drink tea every day."

**Build it on the stem** (the verb without -mAk):

| Stem ends in… | -(I)yor | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| a consonant | **-ıyor / -iyor / -uyor / -üyor** (4-way I) | bak·**ıyor**, gel·**iyor**, otur·**uyor**, gör·**üyor** |
| a vowel | **-yor** (no extra vowel) | oku·**yor**, uyu·**yor** |
| **a** or **e** | the a/e turns into **ı / i / u / ü**, following the vowel **before** it | başla → başl**ı**yor, bekle → bekl**i**yor, oyna → oyn**u**yor, söyle → söyl**ü**yor |

**"This one never changes":** only the first vowel harmonises. **-yor** is always *-yor*, so the person endings are always the **u**-forms:

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| ben | gel·iyor·**um** | I'm coming |
| sen | gel·iyor·**sun** | you're coming |
| o | gel·iyor | he / she is coming |
| biz | gel·iyor·**uz** | we're coming |
| siz | gel·iyor·**sunuz** | you're coming |
| onlar | gel·iyor(·**lar**) | they're coming |

No buffer y: -yor ends in a consonant (gel·iyor·**um**, not ~~geliyoryum~~).

**Stem changes:**
- t → d only in **gitmek** and **etmek**: *gidiyor*, *ediyor*. Not in other verbs: *atmak → atıyor*, *yatmak → yatıyor*.
- **yemek → yiyor**, **demek → diyor**.

Objects stay general in this lesson: *Kitap okuyorum.* "I'm reading (a book)." The ending for a *specific* object comes in L18.

g.L16.prog_neg_q.title: Present continuous: negative & questions
g.L16.prog_neg_q.reference:
**Negative: stem + -mI + -yor.** The negative ending is **-mA**, but before -yor its vowel changes like a stem-final a/e in L15. So in practice it is **-mı / -mi / -mu / -mü**, following the last vowel of the stem:

| Verb | Negative |
|---|---|
| gel·mek | gel·**mi**·yor·um "I'm not coming" |
| bak·mak | bak·**mı**·yor·um |
| oku·mak | oku·**mu**·yor·um |
| gör·mek | gör·**mü**·yor·um |
| git·mek | git·**mi**·yor·um (no t → d: m follows) |

🔊 Stress falls on the syllable **before** the negative: **GEL**miyorum, an**LA**mıyorum.

**Questions: mu after -yor.** *-yor* never changes, so the question word is always **mu**, written separately, and the person endings go on it:

| | |
|---|---|
| Geliyor **muyum**? | Am I coming? |
| Geliyor **musun**? | Are you coming? |
| Geliyor **mu**? | Is he / she coming? |
| Geliyor **muyuz**? | Are we coming? |
| Geliyor **musunuz**? | Are you coming? |
| Geliyor**lar mı**? | Are they coming? |

They: **-lAr stays on the verb** and the question word is **mı** (after *-lar*): *Geliyorlar mı?* (L7: *Öğrenciler mi?*)

**Negative question:** *Gelmiyor musun?* "Aren't you coming?"

Answers: *Evet, geliyorum.* / *Hayır, gelmiyorum.*

g.L17.dat.title: Dative -(y)A: to / toward
g.L17.dat.reference:
**-(y)A** means *to, toward*: **ev·e** "(to) home", **okul·a** "to school", **araba·ya** "to the car".

- **Vowel (A):** last vowel a ı o u → **-a** · e i ö ü → **-e**
- **Buffer y** after a vowel: araba·**ya**, hastane·**ye**

*Eve gidiyorum.* "I'm going home." · *Nereye?* "Where to?" = nere·ye · *buraya* "(to) here" · *oraya* "(to) there".

**Pronouns:** **bana** "to me", **sana** "to you" (irregular), ona, bize, size, onlara. *Bana bak!* "Look at me!"

**Names:** apostrophe, then the ending: *İstanbul'a*, *İzmir'e*, *Paris'e*, *Londra'ya*.

**The word changes before a vowel ending.** -(y)A is the first case ending that starts with a vowel, so three things can happen to the word:

1. **Softening:** final **p ç k** → **b c ğ** (nk → ng) in words of two or more syllables: kitap → kita**b**a, ağaç → ağa**c**a, sokak → soka**ğ**a, dolap → dola**b**a, renk → ren**g**e.
   - Final **t** usually stays: bilet → bilet**e**, bisiklet → bisiklet**e** (a few words do soften, e.g. kanat → kana**d**a; the word card shows it).
   - Most **one-syllable** words don't soften: top → topa, at → ata, saç → saça. A few do: kurt → kur**d**a, uç → u**c**a.
   - **Names never soften in writing**: Ahmet'e, Zonguldak'a (said with ğ).
2. **Vowel drop:** a few words lose their last vowel: şehir → **şehre**, isim → **isme**.
3. **Front words:** *saat* takes front endings: saat**e**.

Compounds that end in *-(s)I* add **n**: buzdolabı → buzdolabı**na** (explained in L24).

**Verbs that take the dative:** **bakmak** "to look **at**" (*Kediye bakıyorum.*), **binmek** "to get **on**" (*Otobüse biniyorum.*).
Remember the **ablative** verbs from L12: **korkmak** "to be afraid **of**" (*Köpekten korkuyorum.*), **hoşlanmak** "to like" (*Kahveden hoşlanmıyorum.*).

g.L18.acc.title: Accusative -(y)I: the specific object
g.L18.acc.reference:
**-(y)I** marks a **specific** direct object: one that you and the listener can identify. It is *not* a "the" ending.

*Bir elma yiyorum.* "I'm eating an apple." · *Elma yiyorum.* "I'm eating apples / an apple." (what kind of thing)
*Elma**yı** yiyorum.* "I'm eating **the** apple." (that one, we both know which)

**Rules of thumb**
1. **Always** with names, pronouns and *bu / şu / o* + noun: *Ali'**yi** görüyorum.* · *Ahmet'**i** tanıyorum.* · *İstanbul'**u** seviyorum.* · *Bu kitab**ı** okuyorum.*
2. A **bare** noun or **bir** + noun is not specific: no ending. *Kitap okuyorum.* · *Bir mektup okuyorum.*
3. An object **without** the ending must sit **right before the verb**: *Her gün kitap okuyorum.* (not ~~Kitap her gün okuyorum~~). With the ending it can move: *Kitabı her gün okuyorum.*

**Forms** (same mechanics as the dative in L17, but a 4-way vowel):

| | |
|---|---|
| after a consonant | ev·**i**, okul·**u**, köpek → köpe**ğ**·**i**, kitap → kita**b**·**ı** |
| after a vowel (buffer y) | elma·**yı**, kedi·**yi**, Ali'**yi** |
| irregular | the genitive and possessive of **su**: su·**yun**, su·**yum** (not ~~sunun~~, ~~sum~~). The accusative *su·y·u*, *ne·y·i* is regular (buffer y). |

**Pronouns:** beni, seni, onu, bizi, sizi, onları · **bunu**, **şunu**, onu.

**Not every verb takes an object in the accusative.** Verbs that take another case keep it, even for specific things: *Kediye bakıyorum.* (bakmak + -(y)A) · *Köpekten korkuyorum.* (korkmak + -DAn). Compare *Kediyi görüyorum.* "I see the cat."

g.L19.poss_sg.title: Possessives (singular owners): my, your, his / her
g.L19.poss_sg.reference:
*my house*, *your car*, *her cat*: Turkish adds an ending to the **thing owned**.

| | after a consonant | after a vowel |
|---|---|---|
| my | ev·**im**, okul·**um** | araba·**m**, kedi·**m** |
| your | ev·**in**, okul·**un** | araba·**n**, kedi·**n** |
| his / her / its | ev·**i**, okul·**u** | araba·**sı**, kedi·**si** |

**Vowel (I):** 4-way harmony with the last vowel, as with *mI* (L7): a ı → **ı** · e i → **i** · o u → **u** · ö ü → **ü**.

**Buffers:** after a vowel, *my* and *your* lose their vowel (araba·**m**, araba·**n**), and *his / her* takes **s** (araba·**sı**).

**Stem changes** (the endings start with a vowel, as in L17):
- softening: *kitap → kitab·ım*, *sokak → sokağ·ım*, *çocuk → çocuğ·u*
- vowel drop: *oğul → oğl·um*, *burun → burn·um*, *ağız → ağz·ım*, *şehir → şehr·im*
- front exceptions: *saat → saat·im*
- irregular: *su → su·y·um, su·y·un, su·y·u*

**Pronouns are optional**, for emphasis or contrast: *(Benim) evim.* "My house." · *Senin kitabın* · *Onun arabası*. Because *-(s)I* means *his*, *her* or *its*, *onun* can make it clear who the owner is.

**Compounds** like *yatak odası* already end in a possessive. It is **replaced**, not doubled: *yatak oda·m* "my bedroom", *yatak oda·n*, *yatak oda·sı* (not ~~yatak odasım~~).

⚠️ **Stress tells two words apart:** *öğretme**NİM*** "my teacher" (the possessive is stressed) vs *öğret**MEN**im* "I'm a teacher" (the copula of L5 is never stressed).

g.L2.harmony.title: Vowel harmony: the two families
g.L2.harmony.reference:
Turkish endings **change their vowel** to match the word. The **last vowel** of the word decides.

In the course, endings are written with capital letters for the vowel that changes: **A** and **I**.

**A: 2-way harmony** (a or e)

| Last vowel | A = |
|---|---|
| a ı o u (back) | **a** |
| e i ö ü (front) | **e** |

**I: 4-way harmony** (ı, i, u or ü)

| | unrounded | rounded |
|---|---|---|
| **back** | a ı → **ı** | o u → **u** |
| **front** | e i → **i** | ö ü → **ü** |

**Only the last vowel counts:** *ki·**tap*** → a → A = a, I = ı · *o·to·**büs*** → ü → A = e, I = ü · *te·le·**fon*** → o → A = a, I = u.

A few words are **rebels**: their last vowel is back, but they take front endings (*saat* "clock", *kalp* "heart"). The app marks them; you'll meet them one by one.

I: a ı → ı, e i → i, o u → u, ö ü → ü

g.L20.poss_pl.title: Possessives (plural owners): our, your, their
g.L20.poss_pl.reference:
| | after a consonant | after a vowel |
|---|---|---|
| our | ev·**imiz**, okul·**umuz** | araba·**mız** |
| your (pl. / polite) | ev·**iniz**, okul·**unuz** | araba·**nız** |
| their | ev·**leri**, okul·**ları** | araba·**ları** |

*our* and *your* are *my* and *your* from L19 plus **-Iz**: ev·im → ev·im·**iz**, ev·in → ev·in·**iz**. Both vowels follow 4-way harmony.

*their* is **-lArI**, the same for every word: ev·**leri**, araba·**ları**. It starts with a consonant, so the word **doesn't** change: *çocuk·ları*, *kitap·ları*.

**Softening review** (only before a vowel): *kitap → kitab·ımız*, *sokak → sokağ·ımız*, *oğul → oğl·umuz*, *renk → reng·i*.

**Plural + possessive:** the plural comes first: *kitap·lar·ım* "my books", *arkadaş·lar·ımız* "our friends".

**Pronouns** for emphasis: *bizim evimiz*, *sizin arabanız*, *onların evi*. With *onların*, people usually use the simple *-(s)I*: **onların evi** "their house".

⚠️ **evleri** has three meanings: *their house* (ev·leri), *their houses* and *his / her houses* (ev·ler·i). Context, or a pronoun (*onların*, *onun*), tells them apart.

g.L21.gen.title: Genitive -(n)In: Ali's, the woman's, whose
g.L21.gen.reference:
**-(n)In** marks the **owner**: *Ali'**nin*** "Ali's", *kadın·**ın*** "the woman's", *ev·**in*** "of the house".

- after a consonant: **-In** → ev·**in**, kadın·**ın**, okul·**un**, Ahmet'**in**
- after a vowel: **-nIn** → araba·**nın**, kedi·**nin**, Ali'**nin**, Ayşe'**nin**
- 4-way harmony, as in L19. Names keep their apostrophe (L11).

**The pattern: owner-(n)In + thing-(s)I.** Both words are marked:

*Ali'**nin** araba**sı*** "Ali's car" · *kadın**ın** çanta**sı*** "the woman's bag" · *ev**in** kapı**sı*** "the door of the house"

The owner can be a possessed noun too: *anne·m·**in** ad·**ı*** "my mother's name".

**Pronouns:**

| ben | sen | o | biz | siz | onlar |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **benim** | senin | onun | **bizim** | sizin | onların |

*benim* and *bizim* are irregular (not ~~benin~~, ~~bizin~~). Compare the regular *siz → sizin*. Irregular noun: *su → suyun*.

**Kimin?** "whose?" = kim + -in: *Bu kimin kitabı?* "Whose book is this?" — *Ali'nin.* "Ali's."

⚠️ *evin* can be *of the house* (genitive) or *your house* (L19). If a possessed noun follows (*evin kapısı*), it's the genitive.

g.L22.compound.title: Compound nouns: Türk kahvesi, otobüs durağı
g.L22.compound.reference:
Two nouns, **no genitive**, and **-(s)I** on the second one = a *type* of thing:

| Turkish | literally | English |
|---|---|---|
| Türk kahve·**si** | Turk coffee-its | Turkish coffee |
| otobüs durağ·**ı** | bus stop-its | bus stop |
| kedi mama·**sı** | cat food-its | cat food |
| araba anahtar·**ı** | car key-its | car key |
| İstanbul Üniversite·**si** | Istanbul university-its | Istanbul University |

The second noun follows L19: buffer **s** after a vowel, softening before the vowel (*durak → durağı*, *bardak → çay bardağı*). You already know some: *yatak odası*, *buzdolabı*, *havalimanı*.

**With or without the genitive?**
- *okul**un** kapı**sı*** "**the school's** door" — one particular school owns it (L21).
- *okul kapı**sı*** "**a school door**" — the kind of door.

**Plural:** -lAr goes in **before** the -(s)I, which comes back as **-I**: *Türk kahve·**ler·i*** "Turkish coffees", *otobüs durak·**lar·ı***.

**Possessive:** the -(s)I is **replaced** (as in L19): *yatak oda·**m*** "my bedroom". **Case endings** after it take **n**: *otobüs durağı·**n**·da* (L24).

g.L23.have.title: Having: possessive + var / yok
g.L23.have.reference:
Turkish has no verb *to have*. It says "**my car exists**": possessive (L19–L20) + **var** / **yok** (L8).

| | Turkish | English |
|---|---|---|
| ✓ | (Benim) bir araba**m var**. | I have a car. |
| ✗ | Araba**m yok**. | I don't have a car. |
| ? | (Senin) araba**n var mı**? | Do you have a car? |
| ? | Araba**n yok mu**? | Don't you have a car? |

The pronoun in the genitive is optional (*benim*, *senin*, *bizim*…). With a noun, the owner takes **-(n)In** (L21): *Ali'**nin** iki çocuğ**u** var.* "Ali has two children."

**How many?** *Kaç* + **singular** noun: *Kaç kardeşin var?* "How many siblings do you have?" — *İki kardeşim var.* After a number the noun stays singular too (L9): *iki çocuğu*, not ~~iki çocukları~~.

**Short answers:** *Var mı?* — *Evet, var.* / *Hayır, yok.*

Compare L8: *Evde süt var.* "There's milk at home." (no owner) · *Sütüm var.* "I have milk."

g.L24.poss_case.title: Cases after possessives: the buffer n
g.L24.poss_case.reference:
After a **3rd-person** possessive (*-(s)I*, *-lArI*), every case ending takes an **n**:

| | -DA in | -DAn from | -(y)A to | -(y)I object |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ev·i | ev·i·**n**·de | ev·i·**n**·den | ev·i·**n**·e | ev·i·**n**·i |
| araba·sı | araba·sı·**n**·da | araba·sı·**n**·dan | araba·sı·**n**·a | araba·sı·**n**·ı |
| ev·leri | ev·leri·**n**·de | ev·leri·**n**·den | ev·leri·**n**·e | ev·leri·**n**·i |

The **n** replaces the buffer **y**: *araba·sı·n·ı*, not ~~arabasıyı~~. *-DA* and *-DAn* always stay **d** after it: *evinde*.

It's the same n you saw in *yatak odası·n·da* (L10) and *Ali'nin evi·n·de* "at Ali's house". Compounds work the same way: *otobüs durağı·n·da* "at the bus stop".

**Other persons: no n.** ev·im·**de** "in my house", ev·in·**e** "to your house", ev·imiz·**den**, araba·m·**ı**.

⚠️ **Same form, two meanings:** *evine* = ev·in·e "to **your** house" **or** ev·i·n·e "to **his / her** house". Likewise *evinde*, *kitabını*. A pronoun makes it clear: *senin evine* / *onun evine*.

**With "to be"** (L11): *Odamdayım.* "I'm in my room." · *Evindesin.* "You're at his house." / "You're at your house."

g.L25.numbers.title: Numbers 11–1000, prices, kaç
g.L25.numbers.reference:
**Tens:** on 10 · yirmi 20 · otuz 30 · kırk 40 · elli 50 · altmış 60 · yetmiş 70 · seksen 80 · doksan 90.

**Build numbers like English, biggest part first, as separate words:** on bir 11, yirmi beş 25, otuz yedi 37, doksan dokuz 99.

**Hundreds and thousands:** yüz 100 · iki yüz 200 · üç yüz elli 350 · bin 1000 · iki bin 2000 · bin dokuz yüz doksan dokuz 1999 · iki bin yirmi altı 2026.

⚠️ 100 is just **yüz** and 1000 is just **bin**, never ~~bir yüz~~ or ~~bir bin~~. From 200 on, the multiplier goes in front: iki yüz, üç bin.

⚠️ Each part is a **separate word**: *yüz yirmi beş*, not ~~yüzyirmibeş~~.

**kaç** "how many" is followed by a **singular** noun, just like a number (L4): *Kaç elma var?* (not ~~kaç elmalar~~), *Kaç kardeşin var?*

**Prices:** 1 lira = 100 kuruş. *On beş lira elli kuruş* = 15.50 TL.

- *Kaç lira?* "How many lira?" · *Bu ne kadar?* "How much is this?"
- *Tanesi kaç lira?* "How much is one / each?" (tane "piece" + the possessive -sI, L19)
- *Elmanın kilosu kaç lira?* "How much is a kilo of apples?"

**Age:** *Kaç yaşındasın?* "How old are you?" — *Yirmi beş yaşındayım.* "I'm 25." The pattern is fixed: number + **yaşında** + "to be" ending.

g.L26.time.title: Time & days
g.L26.time.reference:
**What time is it?** *Saat kaç?* — **Saat** + number: *Saat üç.* "It's three o'clock." *Saat on iki.* "It's twelve."

**Half past:** add **buçuk** "and a half": *Saat üç buçuk.* "It's half past three."
12:30 (and 0:30) can also be said with its own word, **yarım** "half": *Saat yarım.* = *Saat on iki buçuk.* "It's half past twelve."

**At what time?** *Saat kaçta?* — put the locative **-DA** (L10) on the **last word** of the time:

| Time | At … |
|---|---|
| saat bir, iki, yedi, sekiz | bir**de**, iki**de**, yedi**de**, sekiz**de** |
| saat üç, dört, beş | üç**te**, dört**te**, beş**te** (Fıstıkçı Şahap) |
| saat altı, dokuz, on | altı**da**, dokuz**da**, on**da** |
| on bir, on iki | on bir**de**, on iki**de** |
| üç buçuk, on iki buçuk / yarım | üç buçuk**ta**, on iki buçuk**ta** / yarım**da** |

**Days** are written in lowercase: pazartesi, salı, çarşamba, perşembe, cuma, cumartesi, pazar. **Months** too: ocak, şubat… aralık.

Days and parts of the day need **no ending**: *Pazartesi okuldayım.* "I'm at school on Monday." *Akşam evdeyim.* "I'm at home in the evening." The same goes for **bugün** "today", **yarın** "tomorrow" and **dün** "yesterday" (used with the past tense, L30). Months do take -DA: *haziranda* "in June".

*Bugün günlerden ne?* "What day is it today?" — *Bugün salı.*

⏳ Times like *üçü beş geçiyor* "five past three" and *üçe beş var* "five to three" come later: they need endings you'll meet again in an extension pack.

g.L27.ile.title: -(y)lA / ile: with, by
g.L27.ile.reference:
**-(y)lA** means *with* or *by*:

- **by** (transport): *otobüs·le* "by bus", *tren·le* "by train", *araba·yla* "by car"
- **with** (together): *arkadaş·ım·la* "with my friend", *Ali'·yle* "with Ali"
- **with** (a tool or an ingredient): *kalem·le* "with a pen", *süt·le* "with milk"

**Form:** 2-way harmony only (**-la / -le**), and the buffer **y** after a vowel: araba·**y**la, taksi·**y**le. The **l** never changes, so there's no d/t question and the word doesn't change: *uçak·la* (not ~~uçağla~~).

**ile:** the same thing as a separate word. It **never changes**: *otobüs ile*, *Ali ile*, *tren ile*. The suffix is more common in speech; *ile* is common in writing.

**Names** take an apostrophe before the suffix: *Ali'yle*, *Ayşe'yle*, *Ahmet'le*. With *ile*, no apostrophe: *Ali ile*.

**Pronouns** use their genitive form (L21) + -lA:

| | with … |
|---|---|
| ben → benim | **benimle** |
| sen → senin | **seninle** |
| o → onun | **onunla** |
| biz → bizim | **bizimle** |
| siz → sizin | **sizinle** |
| onlar | **onlarla** |

*Kiminle?* "With whom?" (kim → kimin + le).

After a 3rd-person possessive, there is **no** buffer n: *kardeşi·yle* "with his sibling" (compare *kardeşi·n·de*, L24).

**ile = and:** *Ali ile Ayşe evde.* "Ali and Ayşe are at home." Here it joins two nouns, like *ve*.

g.L28.li_siz.title: -lI / -sIz, origin, -CI
g.L28.li_siz.reference:
**-lI** "with" and **-sIz** "without" make adjectives from nouns:

| Noun | -lI | -sIz |
|---|---|---|
| şeker "sugar" | şeker·**li** "with sugar" | şeker·**siz** "without sugar" |
| süt "milk" | süt·**lü** | süt·**süz** |
| tuz "salt" | tuz·**lu** "salty" | tuz·**suz** |

- **4-way harmony (I):** a ı → ı · e i → i · o u → u · ö ü → ü.
- Both start with a consonant, so the word **doesn't change**: *süt·lü* (not ~~südlü~~).
- They work like any adjective: before the noun (*sütlü kahve* "coffee with milk") or as the predicate (*Çay şekerli.* "The tea has sugar in it.").
- Some have their own meaning: **evli** "married" (ev "home"), **tuzlu** "salty".

**Origin:** -lI on a place says where someone is from: **İstanbul·lu**, **Ankara·lı**, **İzmir·li**, **Londra·lı**. *Nereli·sin?* "Where are you from?" — *İzmirli·yim.* "I'm from İzmir."

⚠️ **No apostrophe**: -lI makes a new word, it isn't an ending on the name. *İstanbullu*, not ~~İstanbul'lu~~. (Compare *İstanbul'da*, where -DA is an ending.) The "to be" endings then attach normally: *Ankaralı·yım* (buffer y after a vowel), *İzmirli·siniz*.

**-CI** "person who sells / does": **kahve·ci** "coffee seller, café", **süt·çü** "milkman", **balık·çı** "fishmonger, fisherman", **kitap·çı** "bookseller, bookshop", **gazete·ci** "journalist".

- **C** follows the D rule: **ç** after f s t k ç ş h p (Fıstıkçı Şahap), otherwise **c**.
- 4-way harmony for the vowel, and the word doesn't change: *balık·çı* (not ~~balığçı~~).

g.L29.comparison.title: Comparison: daha, en
g.L29.comparison.reference:
**X is bigger than Y:** *X Y-DAn (daha) büyük.* The thing you compare **with** takes the ablative **-DAn** (L12), "bigger **from** Y":

*At köpek**ten** (daha) büyük.* "The horse is bigger than the dog."
*İstanbul Ankara'**dan** büyük.* "Istanbul is bigger than Ankara."

- **daha** "more" is optional when the -DAn word is there. Without it, you need **daha**: *Bu **daha** ucuz.* "This one is cheaper."
- Pronouns: *benden, senden, ondan, bizden, sizden, onlardan*. *Ben senden uzunum.* "I'm taller than you."
- **çok daha** "much more": *Bu ceket çok daha pahalı.* "This jacket is much more expensive."
- **daha az** "less": *Daha az şeker, lütfen.* "Less sugar, please." **daha çok** "more": *Ali benden daha çok çalışıyor.*

**The most:** **en** + adjective: *en büyük* "the biggest", *en ucuz* "the cheapest", *en iyi* "the best". *En büyük şehir İstanbul.* · *Türkiye'nin en büyük şehri İstanbul.*

**Which one?** **Hangisi?** *Hangisi daha ucuz?* "Which one is cheaper?" — *Bu daha ucuz.*

⚠️ Turkish has no *-er / -est* endings, and the adjective never changes: *daha büyük* "bigger", *en büyük* "biggest". Even *good → better → best* is regular: *iyi → daha iyi → en iyi*.

g.L3.basics.title: This / that, bir, no 'is' in the 3rd person
g.L3.basics.reference:
**bu** "this" (here, near me) · **şu** "that" (near, or pointing at it) · **o** "that" (over there).

*Bu ne?* "What is this?" → *Bu bir kitap.* "This is a book."

**No "is":** the 3rd person needs no verb "to be". *Bu kitap.* = "This is a book." *O Ali.* = "That's Ali." / "He's Ali."

**bir** = "a / an" (and "one"). It is **optional**: *Bu bir kitap.* = *Bu kitap.* There is **no word for "the"**.

**o** = he, she, it **and** that. Turkish has no gender: *O Ayşe.* "She's Ayşe." · *O Ali.* "He's Ali." · *O bir araba.* "It's a car." / "That's a car."

**ne** "what" comes where the answer will be: *Bu **ne**?* → *Bu **bir kitap**.* There is no extra word for the question.

g.L30.past.title: Past tense -DI
g.L30.past.reference:
**-DI** = the past: something that happened and that you saw or know for sure. Add it to the verb **stem** (the dictionary form without *-mak / -mek*):

*gel·mek* → **gel·di** "he / she came" · *oku·mak* → **oku·du** "he / she read"

**Vowel (I):** 4-way harmony with the last vowel of the stem: a ı → **ı**, e i → **i**, o u → **u**, ö ü → **ü**.
*yap·tı, gel·di, oku·du, gör·dü*

**Consonant (D):** after **f s t k ç ş h p** ("Fıstıkçı Şahap") → **t**, otherwise **d**.
*yap·tı, iç·ti, git·ti, kalk·tı* but *gel·di, otur·du, oku·du*

**Person endings (the "k" set).** The past takes a second, shorter set of person endings:

| Pronoun | Ending | gel- | yap- |
|---|---|---|---|
| ben | **-m** | gel·di·**m** | yap·tı·**m** |
| sen | **-n** | gel·di·**n** | yap·tı·**n** |
| o | – | gel·di | yap·tı |
| biz | **-k** | gel·di·**k** | yap·tı·**k** |
| siz | **-nIz** | gel·di·**niz** | yap·tı·**nız** |
| onlar | **-lAr** | gel·di·**ler** | yap·tı·**lar** |

**No stem changes.** -DI starts with a consonant, so the stem stays as it is:
*git → git·ti·m* (compare *gid·iyor·um*), *ye → ye·di·m* (compare *yi·yor·um*), *de → de·di·m*.

**Time words:** *dün* "yesterday", *dün akşam* "last night", *geçen hafta* "last week", *geçen yıl* "last year".

g.L31.past_neg_q.title: Past: negative & questions
g.L31.past_neg_q.reference:
**Negative:** put **-mA** (L16) between the stem and -DI. -mA ends in a vowel, so the past is always **-dI** after it:

*gel·me·di·m* "I didn't come" · *git·me·di·m* "I didn't go" · *oku·ma·dı·m* "I didn't read" · *yap·ma·dı·k* "we didn't do"

The vowel of -DI now follows **-mA**: *-me* → **-di**, *-ma* → **-dı**.

**Questions:** the person ending stays **on the verb**, and **mI** comes after it, as a separate word:

| | present (L16) | past |
|---|---|---|
| sen | Geliyor **musun**? | Geldi**n** **mi**? |
| siz | Geliyor **musunuz**? | Geldi**niz** **mi**? |
| onlar | Geliyorlar **mı**? | Geldi**ler** **mi**? |

In the present, the person ending moves onto *mI*. In the past it **doesn't**: it's already on the verb.
*mI* follows the last vowel of the word before it: *Geldin **mi**? Okudun **mu**? Yaptın **mı**? Gördün **mü**?*

**Negative question:** *Gelmedin mi?* "Didn't you come?"

**Short answers** repeat the verb: *Geldin mi? — Evet, geldim. / Hayır, gelmedim.*

**ne zaman** "when": *Ne zaman geldin?* "When did you come?"

🔊 Stress falls just **before -mA**: **GEL**medim, o**KU**madım.

g.L32.copula_past.title: Past of 'to be': -(y)DI
g.L32.copula_past.reference:
**-(y)DI** = *was / were*. It goes on nouns, adjectives and places, where L5 and L11 put *-(y)Im, -sIn…*:

*hasta·y·dı·m* "I was ill" · *öğrenci·y·di·m* "I was a student" · *ev·de·y·di·m* "I was at home"

**After a vowel → y:** *hasta·ydı, öğrenci·ydi, ev·de·ydi, park·ta·ydı*.
**After a consonant → no y, and the D rule:** *öğretmen·di, yorgun·du*, but *Türk·tü* (k is a Fıstıkçı Şahap letter).
**I:** 4-way harmony, as in -DI.

**Person endings:** the short "k" set from L30:

| Pronoun | hasta | evde | öğretmen |
|---|---|---|---|
| ben | hasta·ydı·**m** | evde·ydi·**m** | öğretmen·di·**m** |
| sen | hasta·ydı·**n** | evde·ydi·**n** | öğretmen·di·**n** |
| o | hasta·ydı | evde·ydi | öğretmen·di |
| biz | hasta·ydı·**k** | evde·ydi·**k** | öğretmen·di·**k** |
| siz | hasta·ydı·**nız** | evde·ydi·**niz** | öğretmen·di·**niz** |
| onlar | hasta·ydı·**lar** | evde·ydi·**ler** | öğretmen·di·**ler** |

**Names** keep their apostrophe: *Ankara'daydım*. **There was / wasn't:** *var·dı*, *yok·tu*.

**Not:** *değil* takes the ending: *değil·di·m* "I wasn't", *Hasta değildim.*

**Questions:** *mI* is a separate word and **carries** -(y)DI and the person: *Evde **miydin**?* (mi + ydi + n) · *Hasta **mıydın**?* · *Öğrenci **miydiniz**?*

🔊 -(y)DI is never stressed: has**TA**ydım, ev**DE**ydim, **AN**kara'daydım.

**Written form idi:** in formal writing the ending can stand as a separate word, *idi*: *Hasta idim* = *Hastaydım*. Recognise it; say *hastaydım*.

g.L33.future.title: Future -(y)AcAK
g.L33.future.reference:
**-(y)AcAK** = *will / going to*. Add it to the verb stem, then the person endings from L5 (the same ones as the present continuous):

| Pronoun | gel- | yap- |
|---|---|---|
| ben | gel·eceğ·**im** | yap·acağ·**ım** |
| sen | gel·ecek·**sin** | yap·acak·**sın** |
| o | gel·ecek | yap·acak |
| biz | gel·eceğ·**iz** | yap·acağ·**ız** |
| siz | gel·ecek·**siniz** | yap·acak·**sınız** |
| onlar | gel·ecek·**ler** | yap·acak·**lar** |

**Vowels:** 2-way harmony (A): *-ecek* after e i ö ü, *-acak* after a ı o u.

**k → ğ:** before a vowel (*-Im, -Iz*) the last **k** softens to **ğ**: *gelece**ğ**im, gelece**ğ**iz*. Before a consonant it stays: *gelece**k**sin*.

**After a vowel → y:** *oku·yacağım, başla·yacağım, bekle·yeceğim*.
In speech the vowel before y is often raised (*bekliycem, başlıycam*), but spelling never shows it: always write **bekleyeceğim**.

**Stem changes (as in the present):** *git → gid·eceğim*, *et → ed·eceğim* (t → d before a vowel); *ye → yi·yeceğim*, *de → di·yeceğim*.

**Negative:** *-mA* + *-yAcAK*: *gel·me·yeceğim* "I won't come" (spoken *gelmiycem*), *yap·ma·yacağım*.

**Questions:** as with *-(I)yor*, the person ending moves onto *mI*: *Gelecek **misin**?* "Will you come?" · *Gelecek **miyim**?* · *Gelecek **mi**?* · *Gelecek **misiniz**?*

**Time words:** *yarın* "tomorrow", *bu akşam* "this evening", *gelecek hafta* "next week", *seneye* "next year".

g.L34.istemek.title: istemek + -mAk: want / want to
g.L34.istemek.reference:
**istemek** "to want" is a normal verb: *istiyorum, istiyorsun, istiyor…* (L15), *istemiyorum* (L16), *istedim* (L30).

**Want a thing:** noun + *istiyorum*: *Çay istiyorum.* "I want tea." / "I'd like tea."

**Want to do:** the dictionary form **-mAk** + *istiyorum*: *Çay **içmek** istiyorum.* "I want to drink tea."

- The infinitive stays exactly as in the dictionary: *gitmek, içmek, yemek, okumak*. No ending is added to it.
- It comes **right before** *istemek*, with its own object in front: *[Çay içmek] istiyorum.*
- Only *istemek* changes for the person and the tense: *Gitmek istiyorum / istiyorsun / istedim / istemiyorum*.

**Not:** put -mA on *istemek*: *Gitmek **istemiyorum**.* "I don't want to go." (*Gitmemek istiyorum* means "I want **not** to go".)

**Questions:** *Ne istiyorsun?* "What do you want?" · *Ne yapmak istiyorsun?* "What do you want to do?" · *Çay istiyor musun?*

This works when **you** want to do something yourself. "I want **you** to go" needs another construction (A2).

g.L35.lazim.title: Need / must: -mAk lazım / gerek; -mA + possessive
g.L35.lazim.reference:
**lazım** and **gerek** both mean *necessary, needed*. They don't change; the verb in front does.

**In general** (no person): *-mAk lazım*: *Çalışmak lazım.* "One has to work." / "It's necessary to work."

**A person needs to:** the verb takes **-mA** (a verbal noun, "going, coming") + the possessive endings from L19–L20, "**my going** is necessary":

| Pronoun | gitmek | çalışmak |
|---|---|---|
| (benim) | git·me·**m** lazım | çalış·ma·**m** lazım |
| (senin) | git·me·**n** lazım | çalış·ma·**n** lazım |
| (onun) | git·me·**si** lazım | çalış·ma·**sı** lazım |
| (bizim) | git·me·**miz** lazım | çalış·ma·**mız** lazım |
| (sizin) | git·me·**niz** lazım | çalış·ma·**nız** lazım |
| (onların) | git·me·**leri** lazım | çalış·ma·**ları** lazım |

-mA ends in a vowel, so the possessive takes its short form: *-m, -n, -sI*. A name or pronoun goes in the genitive (L21): *Ali'nin gelmesi lazım.*

This **-mA** is not the negative **-mA** (L16): it never comes before a tense. *Gitmem lazım* = "I need to go".

**gerek** works the same way: *Gitmem gerek.*

**Questions:** *Ne yapmam lazım?* "What do I need to do?" · *Gitmem lazım mı?*

**Not necessary:** *Gelmen gerekmiyor.* or *Gelmene gerek yok.* "You don't need to come." (*gerekmek* "to be necessary" is a verb.) In casual speech you will also hear *Gelmen lazım değil*.

**Needing a thing:** the person goes in the **dative** (L17): *Bana su lazım.* "I need water." (lit. "To me, water is necessary.") · *Sana ne lazım?* "What do you need?"

g.L4.plural.title: Plural -lAr
g.L4.plural.reference:
**-lAr** makes a noun plural: **kitap·lar** "books", **ev·ler** "houses".

**Vowel (A):** 2-way harmony on the *last* vowel of the word.
a ı o u → **-lar** · e i ö ü → **-ler**

*araba·lar, kız·lar, okul·lar* · *kedi·ler, göz·ler, gün·ler* · *o·to·büs·ler* (only the last vowel counts).

The consonant never changes, and neither does the word: *kitap → kitaplar*.

**No plural after a number or çok:** *iki kitap* "two books", *çok kitap* "a lot of books" (not ~~iki kitaplar~~). The number already says "more than one".

Rebels take front endings: *saat → saat·ler*.

Front last vowel → -ler
First and last vowels differ in harmony: only the last one counts

g.L5.copula.title: Personal pronouns + 'to be' endings
g.L5.copula.reference:
*I am / you are …* is an **ending** on the word: **öğretmen·im** "I am a teacher".

| Pronoun | Ending | öğretmen "teacher" | hasta "ill" |
|---|---|---|---|
| ben "I" | **-(y)Im** | öğretmen·**im** | hasta·**yım** |
| sen "you" | **-sIn** | öğretmen·**sin** | hasta·**sın** |
| o "he / she / it" | – | öğretmen | hasta |
| biz "we" | **-(y)Iz** | öğretmen·**iz** | hasta·**yız** |
| siz "you (plural / polite)" | **-sInIz** | öğretmen·**siniz** | hasta·**sınız** |
| onlar "they" | **-lAr** (often left out) | öğretmen(·**ler**) | hasta(·**lar**) |

**Vowel (I):** 4-way harmony on the last vowel: a ı → **ı** · e i → **i** · o u → **u** · ö ü → **ü**: *Türk·**ü**m, yorgun·**u**m, iyi·y**i**m*.

**Buffer y:** *-(y)Im* and *-(y)Iz* take a **y** only after a vowel: *hasta·**y**ım, iyi·**y**im* but *öğretmen·im, Türk·üm*.

**3rd person:** no ending (L3): *O doktor.* With **onlar**, -lAr is usually left out: *Onlar öğrenci.*

The pronoun is optional, because the ending already says who: *(Ben) yorgunum.* **siz** is also the polite "you".

**Stress:** the ending is never stressed. Stress stays on the syllable before it: *öğret**MEN**im, has**TA**yım*.

Fixed phrase (explained in L28): *Nerelisin?* "Where are you from?" — *İngilizim. / Amerikalıyım.*

After a consonant: no buffer (yorgunum, Türküm)

-(y)Iz: we are (hastayız, yorgunuz)

g.L6.degil.title: Negation of 'to be': değil
g.L6.degil.reference:
**değil** = "not". It comes **after** the word, as a separate word, and the "to be" ending (L5) moves onto it:

| Pronoun | Form | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| ben | öğretmen **değilim** | I'm not a teacher |
| sen | öğretmen **değilsin** | you aren't a teacher |
| o | öğretmen **değil** | he / she isn't a teacher |
| biz | öğretmen **değiliz** | we aren't teachers |
| siz | öğretmen **değilsiniz** | you (pl. / polite) aren't teachers |
| onlar | öğretmen **değil(ler)** | they aren't teachers |

**değil never harmonises** with the word before it: *hasta değilim*, *yorgun değiliz*, *Türk değilsin*. The endings always have **i**, because *değil* ends in **i·l**.

**No buffer y:** *değil* ends in a consonant: *değil·im*, not ~~değilyim~~.

The word before *değil* stays bare: *hasta değilim*, not ~~hastayım değil~~.

*Bu bir kitap değil.* "This isn't a book."

patterns.description: The person ending goes on değil: değilim, değilsin, değiliz…
değil never changes: hasta değilim, yorgun değiliz
The word before değil takes no ending: hasta değilim

g.L7.question.title: Questions with mI
g.L7.question.reference:
**Yes/no questions** use the particle **mI**. It is written as a **separate word**, right after the word you ask about:

*Hasta **mı**?* "Is he / she ill?" · *Öğrenci **misin**?* "Are you a student?"

**Vowel (I):** 4-way harmony with the **last vowel of the word before it**: a ı → **mı** · e i → **mi** · o u → **mu** · ö ü → **mü**. The **m** never changes.

**Person endings go on mI** (with the buffer y after its vowel):

| Pronoun | hasta "ill" | öğrenci "student" |
|---|---|---|
| ben | hasta **mıyım**? | öğrenci **miyim**? |
| sen | hasta **mısın**? | öğrenci **misin**? |
| o | hasta **mı**? | öğrenci **mi**? |
| biz | hasta **mıyız**? | öğrenci **miyiz**? |
| siz | hasta **mısınız**? | öğrenci **misiniz**? |
| onlar | hasta**lar mı**? | öğrenci**ler mi**? |

In the 3rd person plural, **-lAr stays on the word**: *Öğrenciler mi?* (not ~~Öğrenci miler?~~).

**Stress** falls on the syllable **before** mI: *has**TA** mı?*, *öğren**Cİ** misin?*. mI itself is never stressed.

**Question words** ask on their own and **never** take mI: **ne** "what", **kim** "who", **nerede** "where", **nasıl** "how". *Ali nerede?* (not ~~Ali nerede mi?~~). With a question word, the ending goes on it: *Nasılsın?* "How are you?" — *İyiyim.* "I'm fine."

g.L8.varyok.title: var / yok: there is / there isn't
g.L8.varyok.reference:
**var** = "there is / there are" · **yok** = "there isn't / there aren't". They come at the **end**:

*Çay var.* "There's tea." · *Süt yok.* "There's no milk."

**Question:** add **mı** (L7): *Çay var mı?* "Is there any tea?" · *Kahve yok mu?* "Isn't there any coffee?"

**Answer with var or yok**, not with evet / hayır alone: *Çay var mı?* — ***Var.*** / ***Yok.*** (*Evet, var.* and *Hayır, yok.* are fine too, but **var / yok** is the real answer.)

**yok, not değil:** *değil* denies what something **is** (*Bu peynir değil.* "This isn't cheese."); *yok* says something **isn't there** (*Peynir yok.* "There's no cheese.").

The noun stays singular after *çok* and numbers, as in L4: *Çok ekmek var.* "There's a lot of bread."

g.L9.adj_num.title: Adjectives & numbers 1–10
g.L9.adj_num.reference:
**The adjective comes before the noun:** *büyük ev* "big house", *kırmızı araba* "red car".

**bir goes between the adjective and the noun:** ***güzel bir ev*** "a beautiful house" (not ~~bir güzel ev~~ in normal speech).

**As the predicate**, the adjective comes after, with no "is" (L3): *Ev büyük.* "The house is big." Compare *büyük bir ev* "a big house".

**çok** + adjective = "very": *çok güzel* "very beautiful", *çok güzel bir ev* "a very beautiful house".

**Numbers 1–10:** bir, iki, üç, dört, beş, altı, yedi, sekiz, dokuz, on.

After a number the noun stays **singular** (L4): *üç kedi* "three cats", *beş kitap var* "there are five books". Number + adjective + noun: *dört büyük ev* "four big houses".

L1.title: Alphabet & pronunciation

cards.body:
👋 **Merhaba!** "Hello!"

Good news: Turkish is written **exactly as it is spoken**. Learn the 29 letters once and you can read any word aloud, and write any word you hear.

cards.title: 29 letters
cards.body:
A B C **Ç** D E F G **Ğ** H **I** İ J K L M N O **Ö** P R S **Ş** T U **Ü** V Y Z

- **No q, w or x.** *taksi* "taxi", not ~~taxi~~.
- **8 vowels:** a e **ı** i o **ö** u **ü**.
- Every letter always has **one** sound. There are no silent letters, except **ğ** (see below).

cards.title: Letters that trick English speakers
cards.body:
| Letter | Sounds like | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **c** | **j** in *jam* | *cami* "mosque" |
| **ç** | **ch** in *church* | *çay* "tea" |
| **ş** | **sh** in *ship* | *şu* "that" |
| **ı** (no dot) | the vowel in *ros**e**s*, lips spread | *kız* "girl" |
| **ö** | German **ö**: say *e*, round your lips | *göz* "eye" |
| **ü** | German **ü**: say *i*, round your lips | *gün* "day" |

⚠️ **c** is never "k" or "s": *cam* "glass" = "jam".

cards.title: The soft g: ğ
cards.body:
**ğ** has no sound of its own. It **lengthens** the vowel before it:

*dağ* "mountain" ≈ "daa" · *yağmur* "rain" ≈ "yaamur"

- **ğ never starts a word.** No Turkish word begins with ğ.
- After **e** or **i** it often sounds like a light *y*: *değil* "not" ≈ "deyil".

cards.title: Dots change the word
cards.body:
Listen to the pairs. One dot or two dots make a **different word**:

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| ı / i | **kır** "countryside" | **kir** "dirt" |
| ı / a | **kız** "girl" | **kaz** "goose" |
| ö / o | **öl** "die!" | **ol** "be!" |
| ü / u | **kül** "ash" | **kul** "servant" |
| ç / c | **çam** "pine" | **cam** "glass" |

So the app never accepts *kir* for *kır*: it tells you which letter is missing.

cards.title: Capital letters
cards.body:
Turkish has **two** i's, and each keeps its dot as a capital:

| small | capital | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **i** | **İ** | *İstanbul* |
| **ı** | **I** | *Irmak* (a name, "river") |

So *I* is never the capital of *i*. Use the letter bar above the keyboard for İ, ı, ç, ğ, ö, ş, ü.

cards.title: Stress
cards.body:
Most words are stressed on the **last** syllable: ki**TAP** "book", ara**BA** "car".

Some aren't, and the course marks them when they come: ***MER**haba*, place names like ***AN**kara*.

L10.title: Locative -DA: in / at / on
not_yet: personal endings on the location (evdeyim) → L11

cards.body:
🐈 **Kedi nerede?** "Where is the cat?"
🛋️ **Kedi kanepede.** "The cat is on the sofa."

Turkish doesn't say *on the sofa*. It adds an ending to the word: **kanepe → kanepe·de**.

cards.title: Meaning: in, at, on
cards.body:
**-DA = in, at, on**. One ending covers all three English prepositions.

| Turkish | English |
|---|---|
| ev·**de** | **at** home / **in** the house |
| masa·**da** | **on** the table |
| çanta·**da** | **in** the bag |

💡 There's no "is" in *Kedi kanepede*. As in L3, the 3rd person needs no verb "to be".

cards.title: The vowel: a or e?
cards.body:
The **A** in -DA follows 2-way harmony. Look at the **last vowel** of the word:

| Last vowel | Ending | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| a ı o u (back) | **-da** | oda·da, okul·da, banyo·da |
| e i ö ü (front) | **-de** | ev·de, bahçe·de, pencere·de |

⚠️ Only the **last** vowel counts: o·to·**bü**s → front → otobüs·**te** (not ~~otobüsta~~).

cards.title: The consonant: d or t?
cards.body:
The **D** in -DA becomes **t** after a *voiceless* consonant. There are only 8 of them:

**F**ı**st**ı**kç**ı **Ş**a**h**a**p** — "Şahap the pistachio seller" → **f s t k ç ş h p**

| Word ends in… | Ending | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| a vowel | -da / -de | masa·da, kanepe·de |
| another consonant | -da / -de | okul·da, ev·de |
| f s t k ç ş h p | **-ta / -te** | kitap·**ta**, mutfak·**ta**, süt·**te**, otobüs·**te** |

✅ -DA starts with a consonant, so **the word itself never changes**: *kitap → kitapta*.

cards.title: Step by step
cards.body:
Two questions, every time: **which vowel?** then **which consonant?**

Plural first, then the location: **ev·ler·de** "in the houses".

cards.body:
📱 **Neredesin?** "Where are you?"
🏠 **Evdeyim.** "I'm at home."

One word, three pieces: **ev·de·yim** = home · at · I am.

cards.title: Location + person
cards.body:
You already know both pieces: **-DA** "at" (L10) and the "to be" endings (L5). Put them in that order: **place · -DA · person**.

| | okul "school" | ev "home" |
|---|---|---|
| ben | okul·da·**yım** | ev·de·**yim** |
| sen | okul·da·**sın** | ev·de·**sin** |
| o | okul·da | ev·de |
| biz | okul·da·**yız** | ev·de·**yiz** |
| siz | okul·da·**sınız** | ev·de·**siniz** |
| onlar | okul·da(·**lar**) | ev·de(·**ler**) |

💡 The pronoun is optional: *Okuldayım* already says "I".

cards.title: Two small rules
cards.body:
**1. Buffer y.** -DA always ends in a vowel, so -(y)Im and -(y)Iz always take **y**: ev·de·**y**im, park·ta·**y**ız.

**2. Harmony keeps going.** The person ending looks at the vowel of -DA:

| -DA gave… | then |
|---|---|
| **-da / -ta** | -yım, -sın, -yız, -sınız, -lar |
| **-de / -te** | -yim, -sin, -yiz, -siniz, -ler |

*park → park·ta → park·ta·yız* · *market → market·te → market·te·yim*

cards.title: Questions and 'not'
cards.body:
Same as L6–L7: the person ending moves onto **mI** or **değil**.

*Parkta mısın?* "Are you in the park?" — *Evet, parktayım.* / *Hayır, parkta değilim.*

They: *-lAr* stays on the word: *Evdeler mi?* (But with *onlar*, people usually just say *Onlar evde*.)

🔊 Stress falls just **before** the person ending: ev**DE**yim, park**TA**yız.

cards.title: Names take an apostrophe
cards.body:
Names of people and places keep their spelling, so an **apostrophe** separates the ending:

*İstanbul'**da*** "in Istanbul" · *Ankara'**dayım*** "I'm in Ankara" · *Ali'**de*** "Ali has it, it's with Ali"

The ending follows the usual rules, based on how the name **sounds**: *Ahmet'**te*** (t after t), *İzmir'**deyim***, *Paris'**te***.

Only **names** get the apostrophe. Language names don't: *Türkçe**de***, not ~~Türkçe'de~~.

🔊 Stress stays on the name: **AN**kara'dayım, **İZ**mir'de.

cards.title: Step by step
cards.body:
Three questions, in order: **which place?** → **-da or -de, d or t?** → **which person?**

- *we · park* → park·**ta** → park·ta·**yız**
- *you · hospital* → hastane·**de** → hastane·de·**sin**
- *I · Ankara* → Ankara·**'da** → Ankara'da·**yım**

cards.body:
🌍 **Neredensin?** "Where are you from?"
🇬🇧 **Londra'danım.** "I'm from London."

*From* is one more ending: **Londra'·dan·ım** = London · from · I am.

cards.title: -DAn = -DA + n
cards.body:
You already know the hard part. **-DAn** is the locative plus **n**, with the same two choices:

| Word ends in… | in / at (L10) | from |
|---|---|---|
| back vowel a ı o u | okul·da | okul·**dan** |
| front vowel e i ö ü | ev·de | ev·**den** |
| f s t k ç ş h p | kitap·ta, otobüs·te | kitap·**tan**, otobüs·**ten** |

✅ The word doesn't change: *sokak → sokaktan*. Names keep the apostrophe: *İstanbul'dan*, *Türkiye'den*, *Paris'ten*.

cards.title: Where are you from?
cards.body:
Add the "to be" endings, exactly as in L11:

| | |
|---|---|
| ben | Londra'dan·**ım** |
| sen | Londra'dan·**sın** |
| o | Londra'dan |
| biz | Londra'dan·**ız** |
| siz | Londra'dan·**sınız** |

-DAn ends in **n**, a consonant, so there's **no buffer y**: Londra'dan**ım**, İzmir'den**iz** (not ~~Londra'danyım~~).

**Nereden?** "Where from?" = nere·den. *Neredensin?* "Where are you from?"

💬 *Nerelisin?* (from L5) is the more standard way to ask; *Neredensin?* is fine in conversation.

cards.title: in or from?
cards.body:
One letter changes the meaning. Listen for the **n**:

- *Londra'**da**yım* "I'm **in** London"
- *Londra'**dan**ım* "I'm **from** London"

cards.title: Preview: verbs that want 'from'
cards.body:
Some verbs take -DAn where English uses another preposition. You'll use them once you have verbs (L14–15); they come back in L17. Just notice them for now:

- **korkmak** "to be afraid **of**": *kedi**den** korkmak* "to be afraid of cats"
- **hoşlanmak** "to like": *çay**dan** hoşlanmak* "to like tea"

L13.title: Clitic de/da vs locative; ve, ama

cards.body:
🙋 **Ben okuldayım.** "I'm at school."
🙋‍♀️ **Ben de!** "Me too!"

This **de** is not the ending from L10. It's a separate little word meaning **too**.

cards.title: de / da = too, also
cards.body:
Put it **right after** the word it adds to, as a **separate word**:

| Turkish | English |
|---|---|
| Ayşe **de** evde. | Ayşe is at home **too**. |
| Kitap **da** çantada. | The book is in the bag **too**. |
| Biz **de** parktayız. | We're in the park **too**. |

**Vowel:** a/e harmony with the word before: a ı o u → **da**, e i ö ü → **de**.

cards.title: It never becomes te / ta
cards.body:
Fıstıkçı Şahap does **not** apply to the clitic. It stays **d**:

✅ Ahmet **de** · kitap **da** · tavuk **da**
❌ ~~Ahmet te~~ · ~~kitap ta~~ · ~~tavuk ta~~

The locative, attached to the word, *does* change: kitap**ta** "in the book", Ahmet'**te** "with Ahmet".

cards.title: Attached or separate?
cards.body:
**Test:** leave the *de / da* out. If the sentence still makes sense, it was "too", so write it **separately**.

- *Ahmet ~~de~~ parkta.* → *Ahmet parkta.* ✓ → **Ahmet de** (too)
- *Kedi bahçe ~~de~~.* → *Kedi bahçe.* ✗ → **bahçede** (in the garden)

Both at once: *Ev**de** **de** kedi var.* "There's a cat at home **too**."

⚠️ Two pairs that even native speakers mix up in writing:

| too (separate) | location (attached) |
|---|---|
| **Ali de.** "Ali too." | **Ali'de.** "Ali has it." / "It's with Ali." |
| **Ben de.** "Me too." | **Bende.** "With me." / "I have it." |

The clitic never takes an apostrophe: *Ali de*, not ~~Ali'de~~ for "Ali too".

cards.title: ve and ama
cards.body:
**ve** "and" joins words: *Ali **ve** Ayşe evde.* "Ali and Ayşe are at home."
**ama** "but" joins two statements: *Ali evde **ama** Ayşe okulda.*

L14.title: Verbs, infinitive, imperative
not_yet: the negative command (Gelme! Oturmayın!) → with -mA in L16, as a chunk later

cards.body:
🐕 **Otur!** "Sit!"
👋 **Gel!** "Come!"

A Turkish verb in its shortest form is already a sentence: an order to a friend.

cards.title: The dictionary form: -mAk
cards.body:
Every verb in the dictionary ends in **-mak** or **-mek** ("to …"). The vowel follows a/e harmony with the stem:

| Stem | + -mAk | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| gel | gel·**mek** | to come |
| git | git·**mek** | to go |
| otur | otur·**mak** | to sit |
| oku | oku·**mak** | to read |
| bak | bak·**mak** | to look |

The part before -mAk is the **stem**. Every verb ending in this course attaches to the stem.

cards.title: Stem = command
cards.body:
Drop -mAk and you have an order to **one** person you say *sen* to:

| Infinitive | Command |
|---|---|
| gel·mek | **Gel!** "Come!" |
| otur·mak | **Otur!** "Sit!" |
| iç·mek | **İç!** "Drink!" |
| ye·mek | **Ye!** "Eat!" |

Between friends and in the family this is normal, not rude.

cards.title: Polite or plural: -(y)In
cards.body:
To a stranger, an older person, or **several** people, add **-(y)In**:

| Stem ends in… | Ending | |
|---|---|---|
| a consonant | **-ın / -in / -un / -ün** | gel·**in**, otur·**un**, bak·**ın**, gör·**ün** |
| a vowel | buffer **y** + ending | oku·**yun** |

The vowel follows 4-way harmony (I), as in *misin / musun*.

**-(y)InIz** is even more formal: signs, announcements, a waiter to a guest: *Lütfen oturunuz.* "Please be seated."

**lütfen** "please" goes at the start or the end: *Lütfen oturun.* / *Oturun, lütfen.*

cards.title: Watch the stem
cards.body:
A vowel after the stem can change it:

- **git → gid·in**, **et → ed·in**: t becomes **d**. Only these two do this (*Teşekkür **ed**erim* is the same *et*).
  Other stems stay: yap → yap**ın**, bak → bak**ın**, iç → iç**in**.
- **ye → yiy·in**, **de → dey·in**: *Yiyin, lütfen!* "Please eat!"

L15.title: Present continuous -(I)yor

cards.body:
📱 **Ne yapıyorsun?** "What are you doing?"
📖 **Kitap okuyorum.** "I'm reading (a book)."

**oku·yor·um** = read · -ing · I. The person endings are the ones you know from L5.

cards.title: Stem + -(I)yor
cards.body:
Take the stem (drop -mAk) and add **-(I)yor**:

| Stem ends in… | Add | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| a consonant | **ı / i / u / ü** + yor | bak·**ıyor**, gel·**iyor**, otur·**uyor**, gör·**üyor** |
| a vowel | just **yor** | oku·**yor**, uyu·**yor** |

The first vowel follows 4-way harmony (I), as in L14's *-(y)In*.

cards.title: -yor never changes
cards.body:
This is the first ending that **ignores harmony**: *-yor* is always *-yor*. So the person endings always follow **o**, and take their **u**-form:

| | gel·mek | bak·mak |
|---|---|---|
| ben | gel·iyor·**um** | bak·ıyor·**um** |
| sen | gel·iyor·**sun** | bak·ıyor·**sun** |
| o | gel·iyor | bak·ıyor |
| biz | gel·iyor·**uz** | bak·ıyor·**uz** |
| siz | gel·iyor·**sunuz** | bak·ıyor·**sunuz** |
| onlar | gel·iyor(·**lar**) | bak·ıyor(·**lar**) |

✅ geliyor**um** · ❌ ~~geliyorim~~ · ❌ ~~geliyoryum~~ (-yor ends in a consonant: no buffer y)

cards.title: Stems ending in a or e
cards.body:
A stem-final **a / e** can't stay before -yor. It turns into ı / i / u / ü, following the vowel **before** it:

| Stem | Vowel before | -yor |
|---|---|---|
| başla | **a** → ı | başl**ı**yor |
| bekle | **e** → i | bekl**i**yor |
| oyna | **o** → u | oyn**u**yor |
| söyle | **ö** → ü | söyl**ü**yor |

Two irregular verbs: **yemek → yiyor**, **demek → diyor**.

cards.title: t → d: only git and et
cards.body:
As in the commands (*gidin, edin*): **gitmek → gidiyor**, **etmek → ediyor**.

⚠️ Only these two. Other stems ending in t keep it: **atmak → atıyor** "throws", **yatmak → yatıyor** "lies down".

cards.title: Now and every day
cards.body:
English has two tenses here; Turkish uses -(I)yor for both:

- *Şimdi çalışıyorum.* "I'm working **now**."
- *Her gün çay içiyorum.* "I drink tea **every day**."

cards.body:
🤷 **Anlamıyorum.** "I don't understand."
🤷 **Bilmiyorum.** "I don't know."

Two of the most useful words in Turkish. Both hide a **not**: anla·**mı**·yor·um, bil·**mi**·yor·um.

cards.title: Not: stem + -mI + yor
cards.body:
Put **m + vowel** between the stem and *-yor*. The vowel follows the **last vowel of the stem** (4-way I):

| Verb | I'm … | I'm not … |
|---|---|---|
| gel·mek | gel·iyor·um | gel·**mi**·yor·um |
| bak·mak | bak·ıyor·um | bak·**mı**·yor·um |
| oku·mak | oku·yor·um | oku·**mu**·yor·um |
| gör·mek | gör·üyor·um | gör·**mü**·yor·um |

💡 *git* keeps its t here: git·**mi**·yor (the t → d change only happens before a vowel).

🔊 Stress falls **before** the negative: **GEL**miyorum, an**LA**mıyorum. Listen for it.

cards.title: Questions: always mu
cards.body:
*-yor* never changes, so the question word after it is always **mu**, written separately. The person ending moves onto it (as in L7: *Öğrenci misin?*):

| | |
|---|---|
| Geliyor **muyum**? | Am I coming? |
| Geliyor **musun**? | Are you coming? |
| Geliyor **mu**? | Is he / she coming? |
| Geliyor **muyuz**? | Are we coming? |
| Geliyor **musunuz**? | Are you coming? |
| Geliyor**lar mı**? | Are they coming? |

⚠️ *They*: **-lar stays on the verb**, and after *-lar* the question word is **mı**.

cards.title: Questions and answers
cards.body:
- *Geliyor musun?* — *Evet, geliyorum.* / *Hayır, gelmiyorum.*
- Both together: *Gelmiyor musun?* "Aren't you coming?"
- *Türkçe konuşuyor musunuz?* "Do you speak Turkish?" — *Hayır, Türkçe konuşmuyorum.*

L17.title: Dative -(y)A + softening & vowel drop
not_yet: the accusative -(y)I (kitabı, suyu) → L18: same mechanics, different meaning
possessive + dative (evime, okuluna) → L24

cards.body:
🚶 **Nereye gidiyorsun?** "Where are you going?"
🏠 **Eve gidiyorum.** "I'm going home."

*To* is an ending again: **ev·e** = home · to.

cards.title: -(y)A = to
cards.body:
Only one question this time, the vowel: a ı o u → **-a**, e i ö ü → **-e**. After a vowel, add the buffer **y**:

| | in (L10) | from (L12) | **to** |
|---|---|---|---|
| okul | okul·da | okul·dan | okul·**a** |
| ev | ev·de | ev·den | ev·**e** |
| araba | araba·da | araba·dan | araba·**ya** |
| hastane | hastane·de | hastane·den | hastane·**ye** |

No d / t here: the ending starts with a **vowel**.

Names: *İstanbul'**a***, *İzmir'**e***, *Paris'**e***, *Londra'**ya***.
Where to? **nere·ye** · here → **bura·ya** · there → **ora·ya**

cards.title: to me, to you…
cards.body:
| | to … |
|---|---|
| ben | **bana** ⚠️ |
| sen | **sana** ⚠️ |
| o | ona |
| biz | bize |
| siz | size |
| onlar | onlara |

*Bana bak!* "Look at me!" · *Onlar bize geliyor.* "They're coming to us."

cards.title: Softening: p ç k → b c ğ
cards.body:
A vowel ending can change the word. Words of two or more syllables ending in **p ç k** usually soften:

| Word | to … |
|---|---|
| kitap | kita**b**a |
| ağaç | ağa**c**a |
| sokak | soka**ğ**a |
| dolap | dola**b**a |
| renk | ren**g**e (nk → ng) |

Remember: with -DA and -DAn nothing changes (*kitapta, kitaptan*). Softening only happens before a **vowel**.

cards.title: Exceptions
cards.body:
- Most **one-syllable** words don't soften: top → **topa**, at → **ata**, saç → **saça**. A few do: kurt → **kurda**, uç → **uca**.
- Final **t** usually stays: bilet → **bilete**, bisiklet → **bisiklete**. (A few words do soften, e.g. kanat → kanada; the word card shows it.)
- **Names never soften in writing**: *Ahmet'e*, *Zonguldak'a* (said with a soft ğ).

The dictionary (and our word cards) mark the words that change: *kitap → kitabı*.

cards.title: Vowel drop and other changes
cards.body:
- **Vowel drop:** a few words lose their last vowel before a vowel ending: şeh**i**r → **şehre**, is**i**m → **isme**.
- **saat** takes front endings although its vowel is a: **saate** (as *saatte* in L10).
- **buzdolabı** already ends in a possessive ending, so it adds **n**: **buzdolabına** (explained in L24).

cards.title: Verbs and their cases
cards.body:
Some verbs choose a case where English uses a preposition:

| Verb | Case | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **bakmak** | -(y)A | *Kedi**ye** bakıyorum.* "I'm looking **at** the cat." |
| **binmek** | -(y)A | *Otobüs**e** biniyorum.* "I'm getting **on** the bus." |
| **korkmak** | -DAn (L12) | *Köpek**ten** korkuyorum.* "I'm afraid **of** dogs." |
| **hoşlanmak** | -DAn (L12) | *Kahve**den** hoşlanmıyorum.* "I don't like coffee." |

Learn the verb together with its case: *-e bakmak*, *-e binmek*, *-den korkmak*.

L18.title: Accusative -(y)I: the specific object
not_yet: bir + accusative 'a certain …' (Bir kitabı okudum) → mentioned only; needs the past (L30)
possessive + accusative (kitabımı, arabasını) → L24
generic objects of sevmek (Çayı severim) → with the aorist (A2); here sevmek has specific objects
oğul with a case ending (oğlunu) → only with a possessive, L24

cards.body:
🍎 **Bir elma yiyorum.** "I'm eating **an** apple."
🍎 **Elmayı yiyorum.** "I'm eating **the** apple."

Same apple, different question: does the listener know **which one**?

cards.title: -(y)I = a specific object
cards.body:
When the object of a verb is **specific** (you both know which one), it takes **-(y)I**:

| Not specific | Specific |
|---|---|
| *Elma yiyorum.* "I'm eating apples / an apple." | *Elma**yı** yiyorum.* "I'm eating the apple." |
| *Bir elma yiyorum.* "I'm eating an apple." | *Bu elma**yı** yiyorum.* "I'm eating this apple." |
| *Kitap okuyorum.* "I'm reading (books)." | *Kitab**ı** okuyorum.* "I'm reading the book." |

⚠️ It's not simply "the": English says *the* in many places where Turkish has no ending (*Kedi bahçede.* "**The** cat is in the garden." is a subject, not an object).

cards.title: Always specific
cards.body:
Some objects are specific by nature, so they **always** take -(y)I:

- **names**: *Ali'**yi** görüyorum.* · *Ahmet'**i** tanıyor musun?* · *İstanbul'**u** seviyorum.*
- **pronouns**: beni, seni, **onu**, bizi, sizi, onları; **bunu**, **şunu**
- **bu / şu / o** + noun: *Bu kitab**ı** okuyorum.*

*Seni seviyorum.* "I love you." · *Bunu alıyorum.* "I'll take this."

cards.title: The form
cards.body:
You already know the mechanics from the dative (L17): buffer y after a vowel, softening, names with an apostrophe. Only the vowel is new: it's 4-way (I).

| Word | to (L17) | object |
|---|---|---|
| ev | ev·e | ev·**i** |
| okul | okul·a | okul·**u** |
| elma | elma·ya | elma·**yı** |
| kitap | kita**b**·a | kita**b**·**ı** |
| köpek | köpe**ğ**·e | köpe**ğ**·**i** |
| Ali | Ali'ye | Ali'**yi** |

Irregular: **su → suyu**, **ne → neyi**.

cards.title: Word order
cards.body:
An object **without** the ending is glued to the verb: nothing goes between them.

✅ *Her gün **kitap okuyorum**.* "I read every day."
❌ ~~Kitap her gün okuyorum.~~

With the ending it can move: *Kitab**ı** her gün okuyorum.* "I read the book every day."

cards.title: Verbs with their own case
cards.body:
The verbs from L17 keep their case, even with a specific thing:

- *Kedi**ye** bakıyorum.* "I'm looking at the cat." (bakmak + -(y)A)
- *Kedi**yi** görüyorum.* "I can see the cat." (görmek + -(y)I)
- *Köpek**ten** korkuyorum.* "I'm afraid of the dog." (korkmak + -DAn)

L19.title: Possessives (singular owners)
not_yet: our / your (pl.) / their (evimiz, eviniz, evleri) → L20
the genitive with nouns (Ali'nin arabası); benim / senin / onun are shown here only as words for emphasis → L21

cards.body:
🏠 **Bu benim evim.** "This is my house."
🚗 **Arabam yeni.** "My car is new."

No separate word for *my*: it's an ending on the thing you own. **ev·im** = house · my.

cards.title: my, your, his / her
cards.body:
| | ev "house" | okul "school" | araba "car" | kedi "cat" |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| my | ev·**im** | okul·**um** | araba·**m** | kedi·**m** |
| your | ev·**in** | okul·**un** | araba·**n** | kedi·**n** |
| his / her / its | ev·**i** | okul·**u** | araba·**sı** | kedi·**si** |

**After a vowel**, *my* and *your* are just **-m** and **-n**, and *his / her* takes an **s**: araba·**sı**.

**The vowel** follows 4-way harmony, like *mI* (L7): a ı → **ı** · e i → **i** · o u → **u** · ö ü → **ü**.

💡 *-(s)I* covers *his*, *her* and *its*: *Evi büyük.* "His / Her house is big."

cards.title: The word can change (L17 again)
cards.body:
The endings start with a vowel, so the L17 changes come back:

| change | | |
|---|---|---|
| softening | kitap → kitab·**ım** | sokak → sokağ·**ım** · çocuk → çocuğ·**u** |
| vowel drop | oğul → oğl·**um** · burun → burn·**um** | ağız → ağz·**ım** · şehir → şehr·**im** |
| front exception | saat → saat·**im** | |
| irregular | su → su·**y**·um, su·**y**·un, su·**y**·u | |

One-syllable words don't soften: *ad·ım* "my name", *saç·ım* "my hair".

cards.title: benim, senin, onun
cards.body:
The ending already says whose it is, so the pronoun is **optional**. Add it for emphasis or contrast:

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| (**benim**) evim | (**senin**) evin | (**onun**) evi |
| my house | your house | his / her house |

*Adım Ayşe.* "My name is Ayşe." · *Benim adım Ahmet.* "**My** name is Ahmet." (and not someone else's)

*onun* is handy when *-(s)I* could mean *his* or *her*: *Onun adı Ali.*

cards.title: Compounds swap their ending
cards.body:
*yatak odası* "bedroom" already ends in *-sı* (more in L22). Don't add a second one: **replace** it.

yatak oda·sı → yatak oda·**m** "my bedroom", yatak oda·**n** "your bedroom"

❌ ~~yatak odasım~~

cards.title: my teacher or I'm a teacher?
cards.body:
*öğretmenim* has two meanings, and only **stress** tells them apart:

| | stress | |
|---|---|---|
| Bu benim **öğretmeNİM**. | on the ending | "This is **my teacher**." |
| Ben **öğretMENim**. | before the ending | "**I'm a teacher**." |

🔊 The possessive is stressed like a normal ending. The "to be" ending (L5) never is: the stress stays just before it.

cards.title: Step by step
cards.body:
Three questions: **vowel or consonant at the end?** → **which vowel?** → **does the word change?**

- *my · kitap* → consonant → -ım → p softens → **kitab·ım**
- *your · araba* → vowel → **-n** → **araba·n**
- *his · çocuk* → consonant → -u → k softens → **çocuğ·u**
- *her · kedi* → vowel → **-si** → **kedi·si**

L2.title: Vowel harmony: the two families
not_yet: what the endings mean: plural -lAr → L4, 'to be' endings → L5
rebels (saat, kalp) beyond a teaser card
sentences (Bu bir kitap) → L3

cards.body:
🏠 **ev** "house" · 🚗 **araba** "car"

Soon you'll add endings to words, and the ending **changes its vowel** to match the word: one ending, two or four shapes.

This lesson trains one skill only: **find the last vowel, and know its family.**

cards.title: Two families: front and back
cards.body:
The 8 vowels split into two families:

| back | front |
|---|---|
| **a ı o u** | **e i ö ü** |

*Back* vowels are made at the back of the mouth, *front* vowels at the front. Say *a* then *e* and feel your tongue move forward.

cards.title: A = a or e
cards.body:
An ending written with **A** has two shapes. The **last vowel** of the word picks one:

| Last vowel | A = | Words |
|---|---|---|
| a ı o u | **a** | ar**a**b**a**, k**ı**z, ok**u**l |
| e i ö ü | **e** | **e**v, k**e**d**i**, g**ö**z, g**ü**n |

This is **2-way harmony**.

cards.title: I = ı, i, u or ü
cards.body:
An ending written with **I** has four shapes. Think of the vowels as a 2×2 square:

| | lips spread | lips rounded |
|---|---|---|
| **back** | a ı → **ı** | o u → **u** |
| **front** | e i → **i** | ö ü → **ü** |

The I copies the **corner** of the last vowel: *araba* → **ı** · *kedi* → **i** · *okul* → **u** · *göz* → **ü**.

This is **4-way harmony**.

cards.title: Only the last vowel counts
cards.body:
Long words can mix families. Ignore everything but the **last** vowel:

- ki·**ta**p → **a** → A = a, I = ı
- o·to·**bü**s → **ü** → A = e, I = ü
- te·le·**fo**n → **o** → A = a, I = u

cards.title: Step by step
cards.body:
Two questions, every time: **which is the last vowel?** then **which family / corner?**

| Word | Last vowel | A | I |
|---|---|---|---|
| masa | a | a | ı |
| su | u | a | u |
| ev | e | e | i |
| gün | ü | e | ü |

cards.title: Rebels (a teaser)
cards.body:
A handful of words break the rule: their last vowel is back, but they take **front** endings. *saat* "clock" and *kalp* "heart" are two.

Don't learn them now. The app marks every rebel when you meet it.

items.prompt: **ev**: which family is its last vowel?
items.translation: ev = house. e is a front vowel.
araba = car. Last vowel a (back) → A = a.
kitap = book. The first vowel is i, but the last one is a (back) → A = a.
göz = eye. ö is front and rounded → I = ü.
okul = school. Last vowel u (back, rounded) → I = u.
kedi = cat. Last vowel i (front) → A = e.
otobüs = bus. The first vowel is o, but the last one is ü (front) → A = e.
kız = girl. ı is back and spread → I = ı.
kedi = cat. Last vowel i (front, spread) → I = i.
gün = day. ü is front and rounded → I = ü.
su = water. u is back and rounded → I = u.
telefon = phone. Only the last vowel counts: o → back family.

items.prompt: **masa**: which family is its last vowel?
items.translation: masa = table. a is a back vowel.
ev = house. e is front and spread → I = i.
araba = car. a is back and spread → I = ı.

L20.title: Possessives (plural owners)
not_yet: the genitive with nouns (Ali'nin arabası); bizim / sizin / onların are shown here only as words for emphasis → L21

cards.body:
🏠 **Bu bizim evimiz.** "This is our house."
🚗 **Sizin arabanız nerede?** "Where is your car?"

*our* and *your* (plural / polite) are the L19 endings plus **-Iz**: ev·im → ev·im·**iz**.

cards.title: our, your, their
cards.body:
| | ev | okul | araba |
|---|---|---|---|
| our | ev·**imiz** | okul·**umuz** | araba·**mız** |
| your (pl. / polite) | ev·**iniz** | okul·**unuz** | araba·**nız** |
| their | ev·**leri** | okul·**ları** | araba·**ları** |

**our / your:** both vowels follow 4-way harmony. After a vowel, the first one drops: araba·**mız**.

**their = -lArI** for every word. Only 2-way harmony at the start: **-leri / -ları**.

cards.title: Softening review
cards.body:
*our* and *your* start with a vowel, so the L17 changes apply:

kitap → kitab·**ımız** · sokak → sokağ·**ımız** · oğul → oğl·**umuz** · renk → reng·**iniz**

*their* starts with **l**, a consonant, so nothing changes: kitap·**ları**, çocuk·**ları**, oğul·**ları**.

cards.title: Plural + possessive
cards.body:
The plural comes **first**, then the possessive:

kitap·**lar**·ım "my books" · arkadaş·**lar**·ımız "our friends" · çocuk·**lar**·ımız "our children"

❌ ~~kitapımlar~~

cards.title: evleri: three meanings
cards.body:
| ev·**leri** | their house |
|---|---|
| ev·ler·**i** | his / her houses |
| ev·**leri** | their houses (not ~~evlerleri~~) |

Context usually tells them apart. A pronoun makes it explicit: **onların evi** "their house", **onun evleri** "his / her houses".

💡 With *onların*, people usually use the simple *-(s)I*: *Onların evi İzmir'de.* "Their house is in Izmir."

cards.title: All six
cards.body:
| | after a consonant | after a vowel |
|---|---|---|
| my | ev·im | araba·m |
| your | ev·in | araba·n |
| his / her | ev·i | araba·sı |
| our | ev·imiz | araba·mız |
| your (pl.) | ev·iniz | araba·nız |
| their | ev·leri | araba·ları |

Pronouns for emphasis: **benim, senin, onun, bizim, sizin, onların**.

feedback.evmiz: **ev** ends in a consonant, so the ending starts with a vowel: **ev·imiz**.

feedback.leri: The last vowel of **okul** is u, a back vowel → **-ları**.
feedback.sı: **okul** ends in a consonant, and *their* is **-ları**: okulları.

feedback.arkadaş·ımız·lar: The plural comes first, then the possessive: **arkadaş·lar·ımız**.

items.note: anneleri 'their mother' vs annesi 'his / her mother'.

feedback.okulunız: Both vowels follow the last vowel of **okul** (u): **okulunuz**.

feedback.oğulumuz: **oğul** drops its last vowel before a vowel ending: **oğlumuz**.

feedback.çocuğları: -lArI starts with a consonant, so **çocuk** doesn't change: **çocukları**.

feedback.saatımız: **saat** is an exception: it takes front-vowel endings: **saatimiz**.

feedback.evmiz: **ev** ends in a consonant, so the ending starts with a vowel: **ev·imiz**.

items.note: evleri: their house / their houses / his (her) houses. All are accepted.

L21.title: Genitive -(n)In
not_yet: compounds without the genitive (okul kapısı, Türk kahvesi) → L22
having with a noun owner (Ali'nin iki çocuğu var) → L23
a case after the chain (Ali'nin evinde) → L24

cards.body:
🚗 **Ali'nin arabası yeni.** "Ali's car is new."

English marks the owner with *'s*. Turkish marks **both**: the owner gets **-(n)In**, the thing gets **-(s)I** (L19).
**Ali'·nin araba·sı** = Ali-'s car-his.

cards.title: -(n)In = 's, of
cards.body:
| after a consonant: **-In** | after a vowel: **-nIn** |
|---|---|
| ev·**in** "of the house" | araba·**nın** "the car's" |
| kadın·**ın** "the woman's" | kedi·**nin** "the cat's" |
| okul·**un** "the school's" | Ali'**nin** "Ali's" |
| Ahmet'**in** "Ahmet's" | Ayşe'**nin** "Ayşe's" |

4-way harmony, as in L19. Names keep their apostrophe (L11). The word can change, as before a vowel in L17: *su → su·**y**·un*, *kitap → kitab·ın*.

cards.title: owner-(n)In + thing-(s)I
cards.body:
Both words always get their ending:

| owner | thing | |
|---|---|---|
| Ali'**nin** | araba**sı** | Ali's car |
| kadın**ın** | çanta**sı** | the woman's bag |
| ev**in** | kapı**sı** | the door of the house |
| anne·m·**in** | ad**ı** | my mother's name |

❌ ~~Ali'nin araba~~ — the thing needs *-(s)I* too.

⚠️ *evin* alone = "your house" (L19). *evin kapısı* = "the door **of the house**": the next word shows it's the genitive.

cards.title: Pronouns: benim, bizim…
cards.body:
You've used these for emphasis since L19. They are the genitive of the pronouns:

| ben | sen | o | biz | siz | onlar |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **benim** | senin | onun | **bizim** | sizin | onların |

**benim** and **bizim** are irregular (not ~~benin~~, ~~bizin~~). Compare the regular **siz → sizin**.

With a pronoun the thing still takes its ending: *bizim ev**imiz***, *onların araba**sı***.

cards.title: Kimin? Whose?
cards.body:
**kim** "who" + -in = **kimin** "whose":

*Bu kimin kitabı?* "Whose book is this?"
*Ayşe'nin.* "Ayşe's." (or *Ayşe'nin kitabı.*)

🔊 A name keeps its own stress before the ending: *Ayşe'nin* is stressed like *Ayşe*.

cards.title: Step by step
cards.body:
*the woman's bag*: **owner** + -(n)In → **thing** + -(s)I

- kadın → consonant → **-ın** → kadın·**ın**
- çanta → vowel → **-sı** → çanta·**sı**
- → **kadının çantası**

feedback.nın: **kadın** ends in a consonant: **-ın**, no n: kadının.
feedback.in: The last vowel of **kadın** is ı → **-ın**: kadının.

feedback.ın: **araba** ends in a vowel, so the genitive takes **n**: arabanın.
feedback.sı: **-sı** is the thing's ending (*his / her*). The owner takes **-nın**: arabanın.

feedback.Alinin: **Ali** is a name, so it takes an apostrophe before the ending: **Ali'nin**.
feedback.Ali'in: **Ali** ends in a vowel, so the genitive takes **n**: **Ali'nin**.

feedback.çantam: **çantam** is *my bag*. The woman's bag: kadının **çantası**.

feedback.Ahmet'nin: **Ahmet** ends in a consonant: **-in**, no n: **Ahmet'in**.
feedback.Ahmetin: **Ahmet** is a name, so it takes an apostrophe before the ending: **Ahmet'in**.

feedback.sizim: Only **benim** and **bizim** end in m. **siz** is regular: **sizin**.

feedback.araba: The thing owned takes **-(s)I** too: Ali'nin **arabası**.

feedback.Ahmet'nin: **Ahmet** ends in a consonant: **-in**, no n: **Ahmet'in**.

L22.title: Compound nouns
not_yet: a case after a compound (otobüs durağında, İstanbul Üniversitesi'nde) → L24

cards.body:
☕ **Bir Türk kahvesi, lütfen.** "A Turkish coffee, please."
🚏 **Otobüs durağı nerede?** "Where is the bus stop?"

Two nouns, and the second one gets **-(s)I**, as if it were "Turk coffee-**its**".

cards.title: noun + noun-(s)I
cards.body:
The first noun says **what kind**. Only the second one takes an ending:

| Turkish | literally | English |
|---|---|---|
| Türk kahve·**si** | Turk coffee-its | Turkish coffee |
| otobüs durağ·**ı** | bus stop-its | bus stop |
| kedi mama·**sı** | cat food-its | cat food |
| araba anahtar·**ı** | car key-its | car key |
| İstanbul Üniversite·**si** | Istanbul university-its | Istanbul University |

The ending is the L19 *-(s)I*, with the usual changes: *durak → durağı*, *bardak → çay bardağı*.

You already know three: **yatak odası**, **buzdolabı**, **havalimanı**.

cards.title: With or without -(n)In?
cards.body:
| | | |
|---|---|---|
| okul**un** kapı**sı** | **the school's** door | a particular school owns it (L21) |
| okul kapı**sı** | **a school door** | the kind of door |

The genitive points at **an owner**. No genitive = **a type**.

*Bu bir okul kapısı.* "This is a school door." · *Bu okulun kapısı.* "This is the school's door."

cards.title: Plural
cards.body:
-lAr goes **in front of** the -(s)I, which comes back as **-I**:

Türk kahve·si → Türk kahve·**ler·i** "Turkish coffees"
otobüs durağ·ı → otobüs durak·**lar·ı** "bus stops"

❌ ~~Türk kahvesiler~~

cards.title: Owner + compound
cards.body:
A compound can have an owner too. The -(s)I covers both:

*Ali'nin araba anahtarı* "Ali's car key" (not ~~araba anahtarısı~~)

And with *my*: the -(s)I is **replaced** (L19): *yatak oda**m*** "my bedroom", *araba anahtar**ım*** "my car key".
