L23.title: Having: possessive + var/yok
not_yet: prices and 'Kaç lira?' → L25
had / didn't have (vardı, yoktu) → L32
a case after the possessive (evinde bahçe var) → L24

cards.body:
👫 **Benim bir kardeşim var.** "I have a sibling."
🚗 **Arabam yok.** "I don't have a car."

Turkish has no verb *to have*. It says "**my sibling exists**": possessive + **var** (L8).

cards.title: possessive + var / yok
cards.body:
| | Turkish | English |
|---|---|---|
| ✓ | Araba**m var**. | I have a car. |
| ✗ | Araba**m yok**. | I don't have a car. |
| ? | Araba**n var mı**? | Do you have a car? |
| ? | Araba**n yok mu**? | Don't you have a car? |

The person is in the **possessive**: araba·**m** (I), araba·**n** (you), araba·**sı** (he / she), araba·**mız** (we)…

The pronoun is optional, as in L19: *(Senin) araban var mı?*

❌ *I don't have* is **yok**, never ~~değil~~.

cards.title: Someone else has
cards.body:
With a noun, the owner takes **-(n)In** (L21):

*Ali'**nin** iki çocuğ**u** var.* "Ali has two children."
*Ayşe'**nin** kedi**si** yok.* "Ayşe doesn't have a cat."
*Anne·m·**in** bir kedi**si** var.* "My mother has a cat."

cards.title: Kaç? How many?
cards.body:
**kaç** + a **singular** noun:

*Kaç kardeşin var?* "How many siblings do you have?"
*İki kardeşim var.* "I have two siblings."

After *kaç* or a number, the noun stays singular (L9): *iki çocuğu*, not ~~iki çocukları~~.

**Short answers:** *Var mı?* — *Evet, var.* / *Hayır, yok.*

cards.title: There is vs I have
cards.body:
| | |
|---|---|
| *Evde süt var.* (L8) | There's milk at home. (no owner) |
| *Süt**üm** var.* | **I have** milk. |

The only difference is the possessive ending.

cards.body:
🐈 **Kedi Ali'nin evinde.** "The cat is at Ali's house."

ev·i "his house" + -de "at" → ev·i·**n**·de. A small **n** appears between the two endings.

cards.title: After -(s)I: add n
cards.body:
After a **3rd-person** possessive, every case ending takes **n**:

| | in | from | to | object |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ev·i | ev·i·**n**·de | ev·i·**n**·den | ev·i·**n**·e | ev·i·**n**·i |
| araba·sı | araba·sı·**n**·da | araba·sı·**n**·dan | araba·sı·**n**·a | araba·sı·**n**·ı |
| okul·u | okul·u·**n**·da | okul·u·**n**·dan | okul·u·**n**·a | okul·u·**n**·u |

The **n** takes the place of the buffer **y**: araba·sı·**n**·ı, not ~~arabasıyı~~. And -DA stays **d** after it.

cards.title: You've seen it before
cards.body:
The same **n** follows every *-(s)I*:

- their: ev·leri·**n**·de "at their house" · *Onlar evlerinde.*
- compounds: yatak odası·**n**·da (L10!) · otobüs durağı·**n**·da
- the L21 chain: Ali'nin ev·i·**n**·de

cards.title: my, your, our: no n
cards.body:
The other persons just add the case:

| | |
|---|---|
| ev·im·**de** | in my house |
| ev·in·**e** | to your house |
| ev·imiz·**den** | from our house |
| araba·m·**ı** | my car (object) |

With "to be" (L11): *Odamdayım.* "I'm in my room." = oda·m·da·yım.

cards.title: evine: your house or his?
cards.body:
Two different chains give the same word:

ev·**in**·e "to **your** house" · ev·**i·n**·e "to **his / her** house"

The same goes for *evinde*, *kitabını*… A pronoun makes it clear:
*Senin evine gidiyorum.* / *Onun evine gidiyorum.*

cards.title: Where does it hurt?
cards.body:
The body part takes the possessive, and **ağrımak** "to hurt" goes in the present continuous (L15):

*Başım ağrıyor.* "My head hurts." · *Ayşe'nin kulağı ağrıyor.* "Ayşe's ear hurts."

The doctor asks *Neren ağrıyor?* "Where does it hurt?" (nere·n "your where"). Answer: *Geçmiş olsun!* "Get well soon!"

cards.title: Build the chain
cards.body:
**word · possessive · (n) · case**

- araba · sı · **n** · ı → *arabasını* "his car" (object)
- okul · u · **n** · a → *okuluna* "to her school"
- ev · im · de → *evimde* "in my house" (no n)

L25.title: Numbers 11–1000, prices, kaç
not_yet: ordinals (birinci, ikinci) and dates (ayın kaçı?) → later extension

cards.body:
🛍️ **Bu ne kadar?** "How much is this?"
🏷️ **Yüz yirmi beş lira.** "125 lira."

Big numbers in Turkish are built like a sum, biggest part first: **yüz · yirmi · beş** = 100 + 20 + 5.

cards.title: The tens
cards.body:
You know 1–10 (L9). Learn eight new words and you can count to 99:

| | | | |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 **on** | 20 **yirmi** | 30 **otuz** | 40 **kırk** |
| 50 **elli** | 60 **altmış** | 70 **yetmiş** | 80 **seksen** |
| 90 **doksan** | | | |

Then just add the units, as **separate words**: on **bir** 11, yirmi **beş** 25, otuz **yedi** 37, doksan **dokuz** 99.

⚠️ Listen carefully: **sekiz** 8 · **on sekiz** 18 · **seksen** 80.

cards.title: 100 and 1000
cards.body:
**yüz** = 100 and **bin** = 1000. No *bir* in front:

✅ yüz · bin
❌ ~~bir yüz~~ · ~~bir bin~~

From 200, the multiplier goes first: **iki yüz** 200, **üç yüz elli** 350, **iki bin** 2000.

| | |
|---|---|
| 125 | yüz yirmi beş |
| 1453 | bin dört yüz elli üç |
| 2026 | iki bin yirmi altı |

Every part is a **separate word**: *yüz yirmi beş*, not ~~yüzyirmibeş~~.

cards.title: kaç = how many
cards.body:
**kaç** works like a number, so the noun after it stays **singular** (as in L4: *iki kitap*):

- **Kaç elma** var? "How many apples are there?" (not ~~kaç elmalar~~)
- **Kaç kardeşin** var? — İki kardeşim var.

**Age** uses a fixed pattern: number + **yaşında** + "to be":

- *Kaç yaşındasın?* "How old are you?"
- *Yirmi beş yaşındayım.* "I'm 25." · *Ahmet yetmiş iki yaşında.*

cards.title: Prices
cards.body:
1 **lira** = 100 **kuruş**. Say the lira, then the kuruş: **On beş lira elli kuruş.** = 15.50 TL.

Three ways to ask:

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kaç lira?** | How many lira? |
| **Bu ne kadar?** | How much is this? |
| **Tanesi kaç lira?** | How much is one / each? |

At the market, prices are per kilo: *Elmanın kilosu kaç lira?* "How much is a kilo of apples?" — *Kırk lira.*

items.note: Ear training: sekiz / on sekiz / seksen.

L26.title: Time & days
not_yet: minutes past / to (üçü beş geçiyor, üçe beş var) → extension pack (needs the accusative and dative on times)

cards.body:
🕒 **Saat kaç?** "What time is it?" — **Saat üç.** "It's three."
🎬 **Film saat kaçta?** "What time is the film?" — **Saat dokuzda.** "At nine."

*What time?* and *At what time?* differ by one ending you already know: **-DA**.

cards.title: What time is it?
cards.body:
**Saat** "hour, clock" + the number:

| | |
|---|---|
| 🕒 3:00 | Saat **üç**. |
| 🕞 3:30 | Saat üç **buçuk**. |
| 🕛 12:00 | Saat **on iki**. |
| 🕧 12:30 | Saat on iki buçuk. = Saat **yarım**. |

**buçuk** = "and a half". **12:30** (and 0:30) can also be said with its own word, **yarım** "half": *Saat yarım.* = *Saat on iki buçuk.* For 1:30, it's always *Saat bir buçuk*.

cards.title: At what time? → -DA
cards.body:
**Saat kaçta?** "At what time?" Put **-DA** (L10) on the **last word** of the time. Same two questions as always: *which vowel? which consonant?*

| | at … |
|---|---|
| bir, iki, yedi, sekiz | bir**de**, iki**de**, yedi**de**, sekiz**de** |
| üç, dört, beş | üç**te**, dört**te**, beş**te** (Fıstıkçı Şahap!) |
| altı, dokuz, on | altı**da**, dokuz**da**, on**da** |
| on bir, on iki | on bir**de**, on iki**de** |
| üç buçuk, on iki buçuk / yarım | üç buçuk**ta**, on iki buçuk**ta** / yarım**da** |

*Saat yedide kalkıyorum.* "I get up at seven."

cards.title: Days: no ending
cards.body:
Hours need **-DA**, but days and parts of the day need **nothing**:

- **Pazartesi** okuldayım. "I'm at school **on** Monday."
- **Akşam** evdeyim. "I'm at home **in** the evening."
- **Yarın sabah** İzmir'e gidiyorum. "I'm going to İzmir tomorrow morning."

Days and months are written in **lowercase**: *pazartesi, salı, çarşamba, perşembe, cuma, cumartesi, pazar*.

*Bugün günlerden ne?* "What day is it today?" — *Bugün salı.*

cards.title: Good to know
cards.body:
- **pazar** means both *Sunday* and *bazaar*: *Pazar günü pazara gidiyoruz.* "On Sunday we go to the bazaar."
- Timetables use the 24-hour clock: *saat on dokuz* = 19:00.
- **dün** "yesterday" needs the past tense, so you'll use it from L30.
- *üçü beş geçiyor* "five past three" and *üçe beş var* "five to three" come later, in an extension pack.

L27.title: -(y)lA / ile
not_yet: hakkında 'about', -(y)ArAk 'by doing' → A2
birlikte as a full postposition drill (Ali'yle birlikte) → shown once, reviewed later
the colloquial forms benle, onla → mentioned only as non-standard

cards.body:
🚌 **Okula otobüsle gidiyorum.** "I go to school **by** bus."
🧑‍🤝‍🧑 **Arkadaşımla parktayım.** "I'm in the park **with** my friend."

English needs two words, *by* and *with*. Turkish uses one ending: **-(y)lA**.

cards.title: -(y)lA = with, by
cards.body:
Only **two** forms, **-la / -le** (2-way harmony, like -DA), plus the buffer **y** after a vowel:

| Word ends in… | Ending | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| consonant, back vowel | **-la** | uçak·**la**, arkadaşım·**la** |
| consonant, front vowel | **-le** | otobüs·**le**, tren·**le**, kalem·**le** |
| vowel a ı o u | **-yla** | araba·**yla**, metro·**yla** |
| vowel e i ö ü | **-yle** | taksi·**yle**, anne·**yle** |

✅ The **l** never changes (no d/t question) and the word stays as it is: *uçak → uçakla*, not ~~uçağla~~.

It covers: **by** (*trenle* "by train"), **with** someone (*Ali'yle* "with Ali") and **with** something (*kalemle* "with a pen", *sütle* "with milk").

cards.title: ile: the separate word
cards.body:
**ile** is the same thing written as a separate word. It **never changes**, whatever the vowels:

| suffix | separate |
|---|---|
| otobüs**le** | otobüs **ile** |
| uçak**la** | uçak **ile** |
| Ali'**yle** | Ali **ile** |

Names take an apostrophe before the suffix (*Ali'yle, Ayşe'yle, Ahmet'le*), but not before *ile*.

The suffix is more common when speaking; *ile* is common in writing.

cards.title: With me, with you
cards.body:
Pronouns add -lA to their **genitive** form (L21):

| | | with … |
|---|---|---|
| ben | benim | **benimle** |
| sen | senin | **seninle** |
| o | onun | **onunla** |
| biz | bizim | **bizimle** |
| siz | sizin | **sizinle** |
| onlar | — | **onlarla** |

**Kiminle?** "With whom?" (kim → kimin → kiminle). *Kiminle gidiyorsun? — Annemle.*

💬 You'll hear *benle, onla* in casual speech, but write **benimle, onunla**.

cards.title: ile = and; birlikte
cards.body:
Between two nouns, **ile** can mean *and*, like **ve** (L13):

*Ali **ile** Ayşe evde.* "Ali and Ayşe are at home."

After a possessive (*kardeşi* "her sibling"), -(y)lA takes the buffer **y**, not the **n** of L24: *Ayşe kardeşi**yle** parkta.*

**birlikte** "together" often follows: *Ayşe'yle birlikte okula gidiyoruz.* "Ayşe and I go to school together."

L28.title: -lI / -sIz, origin, -CI
not_yet: -lIk (gözlük, kitaplık) and -CA (Türkçe as a pattern) → A2 word-building
-sIz + person endings in long chains (parasızım) → later review

cards.body:
🍵 **Çay şekerli mi?** "Is there sugar in the tea?" — **Hayır, şekersiz.** "No, without sugar."
🌍 **Nerelisin?** "Where are you from?" — **İzmirliyim.** "I'm from İzmir."

Remember *Nerelisin?* from L5? Now you can take it apart: **nere·li·sin**.

cards.title: -lI with, -sIz without
cards.body:
Two endings that turn a noun into an adjective. Both use **4-way harmony (I)**: a ı → **ı** · e i → **i** · o u → **u** · ö ü → **ü**

| Noun | with | without |
|---|---|---|
| şeker "sugar" | şeker·**li** | şeker·**siz** |
| tuz "salt" | tuz·**lu** "salty" | tuz·**suz** |
| süt "milk" | süt·**lü** | süt·**süz** |
| para "money" | para·**lı** | para·**sız** "free, broke" |

They start with a consonant, so the word **doesn't change**: *süt·lü*.

Use them like any adjective: *sütlü kahve* "coffee with milk", *Çorba çok tuzlu.* "The soup is very salty."

cards.title: Where are you from? -lI
cards.body:
On a place, -lI means *from there*:

| Place | Person from there |
|---|---|
| İstanbul | İstanbul**lu** |
| Ankara | Ankara**lı** |
| İzmir | İzmir**li** |
| Londra | Londra**lı** |

⚠️ **No apostrophe!** -lI makes a **new word**; it isn't an ending on the name. *İstanbullu*, not ~~İstanbul'lu~~. Compare *İstanbul'da* "in Istanbul" (an ending → apostrophe).

Add "to be" as usual: *Ankaralı·**yım*** (buffer y), *İzmirli·**siniz***. And **Nere·li·sin?** = where · from · you are.

cards.title: -CI: the person who sells or does it
cards.body:
**-CI** makes jobs and shops:

| | |
|---|---|
| kahve → kahve**ci** | coffee seller, café |
| gazete → gazete**ci** | journalist |
| süt → süt**çü** | milkman |
| balık → balık**çı** | fishmonger, fisherman |
| kitap → kitap**çı** | bookseller, bookshop |

**C** works like **D**: **ç** after f s t k ç ş h p (Fıstıkçı Şahap, the pistachio seller, is a *fıstık·çı* himself!), otherwise **c**. The vowel follows 4-way harmony, and the word doesn't change: *balıkçı*, not ~~balığçı~~.

cards.title: Words with a life of their own
cards.body:
Some -lI words have their own meaning:

- **evli** "married" (ev = home): *Ali evli mi? — Evet, evli. İki çocuğu var.*
- Its opposite is a separate word: **bekâr** "single": *Ben bekârım.*
- **Nereli** "from where": *Nerelisin?*

You already know a few from T4: *Amerika·lı, Kanada·lı*.

L29.title: Comparison: daha, en
not_yet: kadar 'as … as' (Ali kadar uzun) → A2 postpositions
en + plural possessive (en iyisi, en ucuzu) → shown in reviews later
daha with verbs in the past (daha önce) → L30+

cards.body:
🐎🐕 **At köpekten büyük.** "The horse is bigger than the dog."

No *-er* ending and no *than* word. Turkish says "the horse is big **from** the dog", using the ablative from L12: **köpek·ten**.

cards.title: X Y-DAn (daha) big
cards.body:
The thing you compare **with** takes **-DAn**. The adjective never changes:

| Turkish | English |
|---|---|
| At köpek**ten** (daha) büyük. | The horse is bigger than the dog. |
| İstanbul Ankara'**dan** büyük. | Istanbul is bigger than Ankara. |
| Çay kahve**den** ucuz. | Tea is cheaper than coffee. |
| Ben sen**den** uzunum. | I'm taller than you. |

**daha** "more" is optional when there's a -DAn word. Without one, you need it: *Bu **daha** ucuz.* "This one is cheaper."

Pronouns: ben**den**, sen**den**, on**dan**, biz**den**, siz**den**, onlar**dan**.

cards.title: en = the most
cards.body:
Put **en** before the adjective:

- **en** büyük "the biggest" · **en** ucuz "the cheapest" · **en** iyi "the best"
- *En büyük şehir İstanbul.* "The biggest city is Istanbul."
- *Türkiye'nin en büyük şehri İstanbul.* "Turkey's biggest city is Istanbul."
- *En iyi arkadaşım Ayşe.* "My best friend is Ayşe."

Even *good → better → best* is regular: **iyi → daha iyi → en iyi**.

cards.title: Which one?
cards.body:
**Hangisi?** "Which one?"

- *Hangisi daha ucuz?* "Which one is cheaper?" — *Bu daha ucuz.*
- *Hangisi daha iyi, çay mı kahve mi?* "Which is better, tea or coffee?"

cards.title: much more, less
cards.body:
- **çok daha** "much more": *Bu ceket **çok daha** pahalı.* "This jacket is much more expensive."
- **daha az** "less": *Daha az şeker, lütfen.* "Less sugar, please."
- **daha çok** "more" (with verbs): *Ali benden daha çok çalışıyor.* "Ali works more than me."

L3.title: This / that, bir, no 'is' in the 3rd person
not_yet: plurals (kitaplar) → L4
I am / you are (öğretmenim) → L5
yes/no questions with mI (Bu kitap mı?) → L7
adjective + bir + noun (güzel bir ev) → L9

cards.body:
📕 **Bu ne?** "What is this?"
**Bu bir kitap.** "This is a book."

Look closely: there's no word for **is**. *Bu bir kitap* = "this a book".

cards.title: bu, şu, o
cards.body:
| Turkish | English | Where? |
|---|---|---|
| **bu** | this | here, next to me |
| **şu** | that | near, or *that one* (pointing) |
| **o** | that | over there, further away |

*Bu bir kedi.* "This is a cat." · *Şu bir sandalye.* "That's a chair." · *O bir araba.* "That's a car."

cards.title: No 'is'
cards.body:
For **he / she / it / this / that**, Turkish needs no verb "to be". Just put the two words side by side:

| Turkish | Word by word | English |
|---|---|---|
| Bu kitap. | this book | This **is** a book. |
| O Ali. | that Ali | That**'s** Ali. / He**'s** Ali. |

💡 *I am* and *you are* do need an ending. That's L5.

cards.title: bir = a, and no 'the'
cards.body:
**bir** means "a / an" (and "one"). Here it's **optional**:

*Bu **bir** kitap.* = *Bu kitap.* "This is a book."

There is **no word for "the"**. *kitap* = "book", "a book" or "the book", depending on context.

cards.title: o = he, she, it, that
cards.body:
Turkish has **no gender**. One word, **o**, covers *he*, *she*, *it* and *that*:

*O Ali.* "He's Ali." · *O Ayşe.* "She's Ayşe." · *O bir araba.* "It's a car."

The context tells you which one is meant.

cards.title: Questions with ne
cards.body:
**ne** "what" sits where the answer will go. The word order doesn't change:

- *Bu **ne**?* → *Bu **bir kitap**.*
- *Şu **ne**?* → *Şu **bir pencere**.*
- *O **ne**?* → *O **bir çanta**.*

🔊 Your voice goes up on **ne**.

items.translation: This is a book.
O Ayşe. = She's Ayşe. o is he, she, it or that.
This is a key.

items.note: bu = this (here); o = that (over there).
bir is optional.

L30.title: Past tense -DI
not_yet: negative and questions (gelmedim, Geldin mi?) → L31
past of 'to be' (evdeydim, hastaydım, vardı) → L32
the -mIş past (geldi vs gelmiş) → A2
past continuous -(I)yordu → A2

cards.body:
🙋 **Dün ne yaptın?** "What did you do yesterday?"
🎬 **Film izledim.** "I watched a film."

One new piece: **izle·di·m** = watch · *past* · I.

cards.title: -DI = the past
cards.body:
Take the **stem** (drop *-mak / -mek*) and add **-DI**. Both letters change, with rules you already know:

**I:** 4-way harmony (like the question word *mI*): a ı → **ı** · e i → **i** · o u → **u** · ö ü → **ü**
**D:** **t** after Fıstıkçı Şahap (f s t k ç ş h p), otherwise **d**

| Stem | Last vowel | Last sound | Past |
|---|---|---|---|
| gel- | e → i | l → d | gel·**di** |
| oku- | u → u | vowel → d | oku·**du** |
| gör- | ö → ü | r → d | gör·**dü** |
| yap- | a → ı | **p** → t | yap·**tı** |
| iç- | i → i | **ç** → t | iç·**ti** |

cards.title: Who? The short person endings
cards.body:
The past uses a **second set** of person endings. They're short: mostly just one consonant.

| | | gel- | yap- |
|---|---|---|---|
| ben | **-m** | gel·di·**m** | yap·tı·**m** |
| sen | **-n** | gel·di·**n** | yap·tı·**n** |
| o | – | gel·di | yap·tı |
| biz | **-k** | gel·di·**k** | yap·tı·**k** |
| siz | **-nIz** | gel·di·**niz** | yap·tı·**nız** |
| onlar | **-lAr** | gel·di·**ler** | yap·tı·**lar** |

⚠️ *we* is **-k**, not -yIz: *geldik*, not ~~geldiyiz~~.
💡 They're the "k" endings. You'll meet them again on the past of "to be" (L32).

cards.title: Good news: the stem never changes
cards.body:
-DI starts with a **consonant**, so the stem stays exactly as it is, even for the verbs that change in the present:

| | present (L15) | past |
|---|---|---|
| gitmek | **gid**·iyor·um | **git**·ti·m |
| yemek | **yi**·yor·um | **ye**·di·m |
| demek | **di**·yor·um | **de**·di·m |

*git* keeps its **t**, and t is a Fıstıkçı Şahap letter → git·**t**i·m: *gittim*, never ~~gidtim~~.

cards.title: When?
cards.body:
- **dün** "yesterday" · **dün akşam** "last night" · **bugün** "today"
- **geçen hafta** "last week" · **geçen yıl** "last year"

*Dün okula gittim.* "I went to school yesterday."
*Onlar geçen yıl Türkiye'ye geldiler.* "They came to Türkiye last year."

🔊 Stress falls on the past ending: gel**DİM**, git**TİK**.

items.translation: I watched a film last night.

feedback.izledım: The last vowel of **izle-** is **e**, a front vowel → **-di**: izledim.
feedback.izletim: **izle-** ends in a vowel → always **d**: izledim.

feedback.gidtim: -DI starts with a consonant, so **git** keeps its **t**, and after t the ending is **-ti**: **gittim** (compare *gidiyorum*, before a vowel).

feedback.okudım: -DI has four forms (ı i u ü): after **u** it's **u**: **okudum**.

feedback.içdim: **iç** ends in **ç**, one of the Fıstıkçı Şahap letters → **t**: **içtim**.

feedback.yedimiz: The past uses the short person endings: *we* is **-k**: **yedik**.

items.translation: We ate rice last night.

feedback.yidik: The stem doesn't change before -DI: **ye·di·k**. (Only the present has *yi-*: yiyoruz.)

items.note: With onlar, -lAr can be dropped: Onlar geçen yıl geldi is also correct.
No change before a consonant: ye·di·m (compare yi·yor·um).

L31.title: Past: negative & questions
not_yet: past of 'to be' in questions (Evde miydin?) → L32
henüz / daha 'not yet' (Daha gelmedi) → later review
Geldim mi? (1st person question) is rare: shown in the table only

cards.body:
📱 **Geldin mi?** "Did you come? / Are you here?"
🙅 **Hayır, gelmedim.** "No, I didn't."

Two pieces you know from the present (L16), in a new place: **-mA** "not" and **mI** "?".

cards.title: Not: stem · mA · dI · person
cards.body:
**-mA** goes right after the stem, as in the present. Then the past, then the person:

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| gel- | gel·**me**·di·m | I didn't come |
| git- | git·**me**·di·m | I didn't go |
| oku- | oku·**ma**·dı·m | I didn't read |
| yap- | yap·**ma**·dı·k | we didn't do |

💡 -mA ends in a vowel, so the past after it is always **-dI** (never -tI): *git·me·di·m*.
The vowel follows -mA: -me → **-di**, -ma → **-dı**.

🔊 Stress falls just **before -mA**: **GEL**medim, o**KU**madım.

cards.title: Questions: the person stays on the verb
cards.body:
The person ending stays where it is, and **mI** comes after it, as a separate word:

| | |
|---|---|
| Geldi**n** **mi**? | Did you come? |
| Ali geldi **mi**? | Did Ali come? |
| Geldi**niz** **mi**? | Did you (pl. / polite) come? |
| Geldi**ler** **mi**? | Did they come? |
| Gel**me**din **mi**? | Didn't you come? |

*mI* follows the last vowel of the verb: geldin **mi** · okudun **mu** · yaptın **mı** · gördün **mü**.

cards.title: Geliyor musun? vs Geldin mi?
cards.body:
⚠️ This is the one difference to remember:

| | present (L16) | past |
|---|---|---|
| sen | Geliyor **musun**? | Geldi**n** **mi**? |
| siz | Gidiyor **musunuz**? | Gitti**niz** **mi**? |

- **Present:** the person ending **moves onto mI**: *mu·sun*.
- **Past:** the person ending **stays on the verb**: *geldi·n*, and *mi* is bare.

❌ ~~Geldi misin?~~ ✅ **Geldin mi?**

cards.title: Answering
cards.body:
Turkish answers with the verb, not with "yes I did":

- *Kahvaltı yaptın mı?* — **Evet, yaptım.** / **Hayır, yapmadım.**
- *Geldin mi?* — **Evet, geldim.** / **Hayır, gelmedim.**

**ne zaman** "when": *Ne zaman geldin?* "When did you come?"

feedback.gel·di·me·m: The negative **-mA** comes right after the stem, before the past: **gel·me·di·m**.

items.translation: Did you drink tea? — No, I didn't.

feedback.içmetim: -mA ends in a vowel, so the past is always **-dI** after it: **içmedim**.

options: Ayşe didn't go to school yesterday.
Did Ayşe go to school yesterday?
items.answer: Ayşe didn't go to school yesterday.

feedback.Geldi misin: In the past, the person ending stays on the verb and **mI** comes last: **Geldin mi?** (Only the present moves it: *Geliyor musun?*)

feedback.gelmetim: -mA ends in a vowel, so the past is always **-dI** after it: **gelmedim**.

feedback.gitmadi: **git-** has a front vowel, so the negative is **-me**: **gitmedi**.

feedback.oku·dı·ma·k: The negative **-mA** comes right after the stem, before the past: **oku·ma·dı·k**.

L32.title: Past of 'to be': -(y)DI
not_yet: possessive + -(y)DI (evimdeydim) → later review
past continuous -(I)yordu → A2
the -mIş past of 'to be' (hastaymış) → A2
idi as a separate word: recognition only (one translate_to_en item)

cards.body:
📱 **Neredeydin?** "Where were you?"
🏠 **Evdeydim. Hastaydım.** "I was at home. I was ill."

*Evdeyim* (L11) = I **am** at home. Add **-(y)DI** and it's the past: **ev·de·ydi·m**.

cards.title: -(y)DI = was / were
cards.body:
It goes where *-(y)Im, -sIn…* went in L5 and L11: on nouns, adjectives and places.

| Word ends in… | Ending | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| a vowel | **-ydI** | hasta·**ydı**, öğrenci·**ydi**, ev·de·**ydi** |
| a consonant | **-dI** | öğretmen·**di**, yorgun·**du** |
| f s t k ç ş h p | **-tI** | Türk·**tü**, büyük·**tü**, sıcak·**tı** |

It's -DI from L30 with a **buffer y** after vowels. The vowel follows 4-way harmony, as always.

cards.title: Who? The short endings again
cards.body:
*was / were* takes the same short person endings as the past of verbs (L30):

| | hasta "ill" | evde "at home" | öğretmen |
|---|---|---|---|
| ben | hasta·ydı·**m** | evde·ydi·**m** | öğretmen·di·**m** |
| sen | hasta·ydı·**n** | evde·ydi·**n** | öğretmen·di·**n** |
| o | hasta·ydı | evde·ydi | öğretmen·di |
| biz | hasta·ydı·**k** | evde·ydi·**k** | öğretmen·di·**k** |
| siz | hasta·ydı·**nız** | evde·ydi·**niz** | öğretmen·di·**niz** |
| onlar | hasta·ydı·**lar** | evde·ydi(·**ler**) | öğretmen·di·**ler** |

Names keep the apostrophe: *Ankara'**daydım*** "I was in Ankara", *parkta**ydık*** "we were in the park".

🔊 -(y)DI is never stressed: has**TA**ydım, ev**DE**ydim, **AN**kara'daydım.

cards.title: There was / not / questions
cards.body:
- **var·dı** "there was" · **yok·tu** "there wasn't" (k → **t**)
- **değil·di·m** "I wasn't": *Hasta değildim.*
- **Questions:** *mI* carries the past and the person: *Evde **mi·ydi·n**?* "Were you at home?" · *Hasta **mı·ydı·n**?*

⚠️ ❌ ~~Evdeydin mi?~~ ✅ **Evde miydin?** Same as the present *Evde misin?*: the ending moves onto *mI*.

cards.title: You may see idi
cards.body: In formal writing, -(y)DI can be a separate word, **idi**: *Hasta idim* = *Hastaydım*. You only need to recognise it. In speech, say **hastaydım**.

feedback.ev·ydi·de·m: Location first, then *was*, then the person: **ev·de·ydi·m**.

feedback.hastadım: **hasta** ends in a vowel, so -(y)DI needs the buffer **y**: **hastaydım**.
feedback.hastaydim: The last vowel is **a**, so -(y)DI is **-ydı**: **hastaydım**.

items.translation: I was at home yesterday.

feedback.evdedim: -DA ends in a vowel, so -(y)DI needs the buffer **y**: **evdeydim**.
feedback.evdeydım: The vowel before is **e**, so it's **-ydi**: **evdeydim**.

options: There was a cat in the garden.
There is a cat in the garden.
There wasn't a cat in the garden.
items.answer: There was a cat in the garden.

feedback.parkdaydım: **park** ends in **k**, one of the Fıstıkçı Şahap letters → **-ta**: **parktaydım**.
feedback.parktadım: -ta ends in a vowel, so -(y)DI needs the buffer **y**: **parktaydım**.
feedback.parktaydıyım: *was* uses the short person endings: *I* is just **-m**: **parktaydım**.

feedback.yorgundık: -(y)DI has four forms (ı i u ü): after **u** it's **u**: **yorgunduk**.
feedback.yorgunduyuz: *was* uses the short person endings: *we* is **-k**: **yorgunduk**.

feedback.dü: **Türk** ends in **k**, one of the Fıstıkçı Şahap letters → **t**: **Türktü**.

feedback.mıdın: **mı** ends in a vowel, so -(y)DI needs the buffer **y**: **mıydın**.

feedback.Evdeydin mi: In a question, **mI** carries the past and the person: **Evde miydin?** (like *Evde misin?*)

items.note: With a plural subject, -lAr is usually left off: Çocuklar bahçedeydi.

feedback.Ankaradaydım: **Ankara** is a name, so it takes an apostrophe before the ending: **Ankara'daydım**.

items.translation: It was sunny yesterday.

feedback.güneşlidi: **güneşli** ends in a vowel, so -(y)DI needs the buffer **y**: **güneşliydi**.
feedback.güneşliydı: The last vowel is **i**, so it's **-ydi**: **güneşliydi**.

items.note: idi is the written form: Hasta idim = Hastaydım.

L33.title: Future -(y)AcAK
not_yet: future of 'to be' (evde olacağım) → A2 (olmak)
future in the past (gelecektim) → A2
the aorist for offers and promises (Yardım ederim) → A2
Gelecek miyim? (1st person question): shown in the reference only

cards.body:
📱 **Yarın gelecek misin?** "Will you come tomorrow?"
🙋 **Evet, geleceğim!** "Yes, I'll come!"

**gel·eceğ·im** = come · *will* · I.

cards.title: -(y)AcAK = will
cards.body:
Stem + **-acak / -ecek** (2-way harmony) + the person endings you know from the present (L5, L15):

| | gel- | yap- |
|---|---|---|
| ben | gel·**eceğ**·im | yap·**acağ**·ım |
| sen | gel·ecek·sin | yap·acak·sın |
| o | gel·ecek | yap·acak |
| biz | gel·**eceğ**·iz | yap·**acağ**·ız |
| siz | gel·ecek·siniz | yap·acak·sınız |
| onlar | gel·ecek·ler | yap·acak·lar |

⚠️ **k → ğ** before a vowel: *gelece**ğ**im*, *gelece**ğ**iz*. Before a consonant it stays: *gelece**k**sin*. (Softening, as in *kitap → kitabı*.)

cards.title: After a vowel: y
cards.body:
| | |
|---|---|
| oku- | oku·**y**acağım |
| başla- | başla·**y**acağım |
| bekle- | bekle·**y**eceğim |

🗣️ In fast speech you'll hear *bekliycem, başlıycam*: the vowel before **y** rises and the ending shrinks. Understand it; **write** *bekleyeceğim*.

cards.title: The four stems that change
cards.body:
The same four as in the present (L15), because -(y)AcAK starts with a vowel:

| | present | future |
|---|---|---|
| git- | **gid**iyorum | **gid**eceğim |
| et- | **ed**iyorum | **ed**eceğim |
| ye- | **yi**yorum | **yi**yeceğim |
| de- | **di**yorum | **di**yeceğim |

cards.title: Not and questions
cards.body:
**Not:** stem · **mA** · **yAcAK** · person: *gel·me·yeceğ·im* "I won't come", *çalış·ma·yacağ·ım*.
🗣️ Spoken: *gelmiycem*. Written: **gelmeyeceğim**.

**Questions** work like the present: the person ending **moves onto mI**:

| present | future |
|---|---|
| Geliyor **musun**? | Gelecek **misin**? |
| Ayşe geliyor **mu**? | Ayşe gelecek **mi**? |
| Geliyor **musunuz**? | Gelecek **misiniz**? |

(Only the past is different: *Geldi**n** mi?*)

cards.title: When?
cards.body:
- **yarın** "tomorrow" · **bu akşam** "this evening"
- **gelecek hafta** "next week" (*gelecek* = "the coming") · **seneye** "next year"

*Gelecek hafta İstanbul'a gideceğiz.* "We'll go to Istanbul next week."

💡 For fixed plans, the present also works: *Yarın geliyorum.* "I'm coming tomorrow."

items.translation: It will rain tomorrow.

feedback.yağecek: The last vowel of **yağ-** is **a**, a back vowel → **-acak**: yağacak.

feedback.gelecekim: Before a vowel, the **k** of -AcAK softens to **ğ**: **geleceğim**.

feedback.okuacağım: **oku-** ends in a vowel, so -(y)AcAK needs the buffer **y**: **okuyacağım**.

feedback.bekliyeceğim: In speech it sounds like *-iy-*, but the spelling keeps the **e** of *bekle-*: **bekleyeceğim**.

feedback.geleceksin mi: As with -(I)yor, the person ending moves onto **mI**: **gelecek misin?**

items.note: git → gid before a vowel, as in gidiyoruz.

items.translation: What will you eat? — I'll eat rice.

feedback.yeyeceğim: **ye-** changes to **yi-** before a vowel ending: **yiyeceğim** (like *yiyorum*).
feedback.yiyecekim: Before a vowel, the **k** softens to **ğ**: **yiyeceğim**.

options: We're going on holiday next week.
We went on holiday last week.
items.answer: We're going on holiday next week.

L34.title: istemek + -mAk
not_yet: wanting someone else to act (Gelmeni istiyorum, -mAsInI) → A2
the accusative infinitive (içmeyi istiyorum) is also heard: not taught, not used as a distractor
the aorist for polite offers (Çay ister misin?) → A2
-mAk with other verbs (sevmek, bilmek) → A2

cards.body:
☕ **Ne istiyorsun?** "What do you want?" — **Çay istiyorum.** "I want tea."
😴 **Ne yapmak istiyorsun?** "What do you want to do?" — **Uyumak istiyorum.** "I want to sleep."

cards.title: A thing or an action?
cards.body:
**istemek** "to want" is a regular verb: *ist·iyor·um, ist·iyor·sun, ist·iyor…*

| want a **thing** | want **to do** |
|---|---|
| Çay istiyorum. | Çay **içmek** istiyorum. |
| I want tea. | I want **to drink** tea. |
| Kitap istiyorum. | Kitap **okumak** istiyorum. |

For an action, use the **dictionary form** (*-mak / -mek*, L14) right before *istemek*.

cards.title: Only istemek changes
cards.body:
The infinitive stays exactly as in the dictionary. Person and tense go on **istemek**:

- Gitmek **istiyorum** · Gitmek **istiyorsun** · Ali gitmek **istiyor**
- Gitmek **istiyoruz** · Gitmek **istedim** (L30)

The infinitive takes its own words in front: *[Antalya'ya gitmek] istiyoruz.* "We want to go to Antalya."

cards.title: Not and questions
cards.body:
**Not:** make *istemek* negative: *Gitmek **istemiyorum**.* "I don't want to go."
(*Gitmemek istiyorum* = "I want **not** to go": a different meaning.)

**Questions:** *Çay istiyor **musun**?* "Do you want tea?" · *Yüzmek istiyor **musun**?*
*Ne yapmak istiyorsun?* "What do you want to do?"

cards.title: You do it yourself
cards.body: *-mAk istiyorum* means **I** want to do it myself. "I want **you** to come" uses another form, which comes in A2.

items.translation: Do you want to swim?

feedback.Yüzüyor: Before *istemek*, use the dictionary form **-mAk**: **Yüzmek** istiyor musun?
feedback.Yüzdün: Before *istemek*, use the dictionary form **-mAk**: **Yüzmek** istiyor musun?

options: Ali wants to watch a film.
items.answer: Ali wants to watch a film.

feedback.içiyor: Before *istemek*, use the dictionary form **-mAk**: **içmek** istiyorum.

feedback.istiyorum değil: To say *don't want to*, make **istemek** negative with -mA: **istemiyorum**. (*değil* is for nouns and adjectives.)

feedback.okumek: -mAk follows 2-way harmony: the last vowel of **oku-** is **u** → **-mak**: **okumak**.

feedback.istiyor film izlemek: The verb comes last, and the infinitive comes right before *istemek*: **Ali film izlemek istiyor.**

items.translation: I want to drink tea.

feedback.içiyorum: Only *istemek* takes the person: **Çay içmek istiyorum.**
feedback.içtim: Only *istemek* takes the tense: **Çay içmek istiyorum.**

L35.title: Need: -mAk lazım / gerek
not_yet: -mAlI 'must' → A2
the negative aorist gitmem 'I don't go': never used here (it sounds the same as the verbal noun)
-mA + possessive as an object (gitmesini istiyorum) → A2
gerek yok 'no need': accepted in answers, not taught

cards.body:
⌚ **Gitmem lazım!** "I need to go!"
💧 **Bana su lazım.** "I need water."

**lazım** = necessary. Literally: "**my going** is necessary", "**to me**, water is necessary".

cards.title: In general: -mAk lazım
cards.body:
With the dictionary form, *lazım* says what's necessary **in general**, for nobody in particular:

*Çalışmak lazım.* "One has to work." · *Gitmek lazım.* "It's time to go." / "We have to go."

**gerek** means the same: *Çalışmak gerek.*

cards.title: Who needs to? -mA + my, your, his…
cards.body:
Swap *-mAk* for **-mA** and add the possessive endings (L19–L20): "**my** going, **your** going…".

| | gitmek | çalışmak |
|---|---|---|
| I | git·me·**m** lazım | çalış·ma·**m** lazım |
| you | git·me·**n** lazım | çalış·ma·**n** lazım |
| he / she | git·me·**si** lazım | çalış·ma·**sı** lazım |
| we | git·me·**miz** lazım | çalış·ma·**mız** lazım |
| you (pl.) | git·me·**niz** lazım | çalış·ma·**nız** lazım |
| they | git·me·**leri** lazım | çalış·ma·**ları** lazım |

-mA ends in a vowel → the short possessives: **-m, -n, -sI**.
With a name, the owner is in the genitive (L21): *Ali'**nin** gel·me·**si** lazım.*

*lazım* never changes. ⚠️ This -mA is **not** "not": *gitmem lazım* = "I **need** to go".

cards.title: Questions and 'no need'
cards.body:
- *Ne yapmam lazım?* "What do I need to do?" · *Ne zaman gelmem lazım?*
- **Not necessary:** *Gelmen **gerekmiyor**.* or *Gelmene **gerek yok**.* "You don't need to come." In casual speech you will also hear *Gelmen lazım değil*.
  (*gerekmek* "to be necessary" is a verb, so it takes -mIyor.)

cards.title: Needing a thing: bana, sana…
cards.body:
With a **noun**, the person goes in the **dative** (L17): "to me, water is necessary".

| | |
|---|---|
| **Bana** su lazım. | I need water. |
| **Sana** ne lazım? | What do you need? |
| **Bize** yardım lazım. | We need help. |

❌ ~~Ben su lazım.~~ ✅ **Bana** su lazım.

cards.title: Want or need?
cards.body:
| | |
|---|---|
| Gitmek **istiyorum**. | I **want** to go. (L34: -mAk, person on *istemek*) |
| Gitme**m** **lazım**. | I **need** to go. (-mA + person, *lazım* stays) |

items.note: Fused: çalışmamız lazım 'we need to work'.

feedback.Benim: With *lazım* + a thing, the person is in the dative: **Bana** su lazım.

feedback.kalkmemiz: -mA follows 2-way harmony: **kalk-** has **a** → **-ma**, and the possessive follows: **kalkmamız**.

L4.title: Plural -lAr
not_yet: bunlar / şunlar 'these / those' → later review
they are (öğrenciler) as a 'to be' ending → L5
numbers 3–10 → L9

cards.body:
📕 **kitap** "book" → 📚 **kitap·lar** "books"
🏠 **ev** "house" → 🏘️ **ev·ler** "houses"

One ending, two shapes: **-lar** or **-ler**. You already know how to choose (L2).

cards.title: -lAr: lar or ler?
cards.body:
The **A** in -lAr follows 2-way harmony. Look at the **last vowel**:

| Last vowel | Ending | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| a ı o u (back) | **-lar** | araba·lar, kız·lar, okul·lar |
| e i ö ü (front) | **-ler** | ev·ler, kedi·ler, göz·ler, gün·ler |

⚠️ Only the **last** vowel counts: o·to·**bü**s → otobüs·**ler** · te·le·**fo**n → telefon·**lar**.

✅ -lAr starts with a consonant, so **the word never changes**: *kitap → kitaplar*.

cards.title: No plural after a number or çok
cards.body:
A number already says "more than one", so the noun stays **singular**:

| ✅ | ❌ |
|---|---|
| **iki kitap** "two books" | ~~iki kitaplar~~ |
| **çok kedi** "a lot of cats" | ~~çok kediler~~ |

cards.title: Step by step
cards.body:
**Which is the last vowel?** → **back or front?** → **-lar or -ler**

- masa → **a** → back → masa·**lar**
- kalem → **e** → front → kalem·**ler**
- telefon → **o** → back → telefon·**lar**

With "no is" from L3: *Kitaplar yeni.* "The books are new." · *Bu kalemler yeni.* "These pens are new."

cards.title: A rebel
cards.body: *saat* "clock, watch" ends in **a**, but it's a rebel (L2): **saat·ler**, not ~~saatlar~~.

items.note: Trap: first vowel o is back, last vowel ü is front.

items.translation: Two books. After a number, the noun stays singular.
A lot of cats. After çok, the noun stays singular.

items.note: Trap: first vowel e is front, last vowel o is back.

feedback.saatlar: **saat** is a rebel: its last vowel is a, but it takes front endings: **saatler**.

feedback.kitaplar: After a number, the noun stays singular: **iki kitap**.

feedback.kediler: After **çok**, the noun stays singular: **çok kedi**.

feedback.iki kediler: After a number, the noun stays singular: **iki kedi**.

feedback.iki kitaplar: After a number, the noun stays singular: **iki kitap**.

L5.title: Personal pronouns + 'to be' endings
not_yet: -DIr (O doktordur) → not taught at A1
negation (öğretmen değilim) → L6
questions (öğrenci misin?) → L7
-lI (Nereli, Amerikalı) as a suffix → L28; here only as words and a fixed phrase

cards.body:
🧑‍🏫 **Ben öğretmenim.** "I'm a teacher."
🤒 **Ben hastayım.** "I'm ill."

No verb "am": Turkish adds an **ending**. **öğretmen·im** = teacher · I am.

cards.title: The pronouns
cards.body:
| | singular | plural |
|---|---|---|
| 1st | **ben** I | **biz** we |
| 2nd | **sen** you | **siz** you (plural, or polite) |
| 3rd | **o** he / she / it | **onlar** they |

💡 **siz** is also the polite "you", for one person you don't know well: a shop assistant, a teacher.

cards.title: The 'to be' endings
cards.body:
| | ending | öğretmen | hasta |
|---|---|---|---|
| ben | **-(y)Im** | öğretmen·**im** | hasta·**yım** |
| sen | **-sIn** | öğretmen·**sin** | hasta·**sın** |
| o | – | öğretmen | hasta |
| biz | **-(y)Iz** | öğretmen·**iz** | hasta·**yız** |
| siz | **-sInIz** | öğretmen·**siniz** | hasta·**sınız** |
| onlar | **-lAr** | öğretmen(·**ler**) | hasta(·**lar**) |

- **o**: no ending, as in L3: *O doktor.* "He's a doctor."
- **onlar**: -lAr is usually left out: *Onlar öğrenci.* "They're students."
- The pronoun is optional: *Yorgunum.* already means "I'm tired."

cards.title: I: your first 4-way harmony
cards.body:
The **I** in these endings has four shapes (L2). It copies the corner of the **last vowel**:

| Last vowel | I = | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| a ı | **ı** | hasta·yım, Fransız·ım |
| e i | **i** | öğretmen·im, iyi·yim |
| o u | **u** | doktor·um, yorgun·um, mutlu·yum |
| ö ü | **ü** | Türk·üm |

cards.title: The buffer y
cards.body:
**-(y)Im** and **-(y)Iz** start with a vowel. Turkish doesn't like two vowels side by side, so after a **vowel** a **y** slips in:

| ends in a vowel | ends in a consonant |
|---|---|
| hasta·**y**ım, iyi·**y**im, öğrenci·**y**iz | öğretmen·im, Türk·üm, yorgun·uz |

-sIn and -sInIz start with **s**, so they never need it: *hasta·sın, öğretmen·sin*.

cards.title: Stress and a fixed phrase
cards.body:
🔊 The ending is **never stressed**. Stress stays just before it: *öğret**MEN**im*, *has**TA**yım*, ***TÜR**küm*.

**Nerelisin?** "Where are you from?" → *İngilizim.* "I'm English." · *Amerikalıyım.* "I'm American." · *Türküm.* "I'm Turkish."

Learn *Nerelisin?* (polite: *Nerelisiniz?*) as a fixed phrase. Its pieces are explained in L28.

cards.title: Step by step
cards.body:
Three questions: **who?** → **does the word end in a vowel (buffer y)?** → **which vowel (4-way)?**

- *I · tired* → yorgun + -(y)Im → consonant, no y → u → **yorgun·um**
- *we · students* → öğrenci + -(y)Iz → vowel, y → i → **öğrenci·yiz**
- *you · happy* → mutlu + -sIn → u → **mutlu·sun**

items.translation: I'm a teacher.

feedback.iyiim: **iyi** ends in a vowel, so the ending needs the buffer **y**: **iyiyim**.

feedback.hastaım: **hasta** ends in a vowel, so the ending needs the buffer **y**: **hastayım**.

feedback.Amerikalım: **Amerikalı** ends in a vowel, so the ending needs the buffer **y**: **Amerikalıyım**.

L6.title: Negation of 'to be': değil
not_yet: questions (öğrenci değil misin?) → L7 and later review
yok 'there isn't' → L8
verb negation -mA (gelmiyorum) → L16

cards.body:
🧑‍🏫 **Ben öğretmenim.** "I'm a teacher."
🧑‍🎓 **Ben öğretmen değilim.** "I'm not a teacher."

"Not" is a separate word, **değil**, and the "I am" ending moves onto it.

cards.title: değil + person
cards.body:
The word stays bare. **değil** comes after it and carries the ending from L5:

| | |
|---|---|
| ben | hasta **değilim** |
| sen | hasta **değilsin** |
| o | hasta **değil** |
| biz | hasta **değiliz** |
| siz | hasta **değilsiniz** |
| onlar | hasta **değil(ler)** |

❌ ~~hastayım değil~~ · ✅ **hasta değilim**

cards.title: değil never changes
cards.body:
The word before it can have any vowel. **değil** doesn't care: its endings always have **i**.

*aç **değiliz*** (not ~~değılız~~) · *yorgun **değilim*** (not ~~değilum~~) · *Türk **değilsin***

It ends in a consonant, so there's **no buffer y**: *değil·im*, not ~~değilyim~~.

🔊 After *e* the **ğ** sounds like a light y: *değil* ≈ "deyil" (L1).

cards.title: Yes → no
cards.body:
| ✅ | ❌ |
|---|---|
| Ben açım. | Ben aç **değilim**. |
| Ayşe evli. | Ayşe evli **değil**. |
| Bu bir kitap. | Bu bir kitap **değil**. |

And a correction: *Ayşe hasta değil, yorgun.* "Ayşe isn't ill, she's tired."

items.translation: I'm not ill. değil never changes, and takes no buffer y.

feedback.Ben öğretmenim değil: The person ending goes on **değil**, not on the word before it: **Ben öğretmen değilim**.

feedback.değilyim: **değil** ends in a consonant: no buffer y: **değilim**.

items.note: With onlar, değil alone is also common: Onlar öğrenci değil.

feedback.değilyim: **değil** ends in a consonant: no buffer y: **değilim**.

feedback.değilız: **değil** keeps its own vowels: the ending follows its **i**, not the a of *aç*: **değiliz**.

feedback.Ben evliyim değil: The person ending goes on **değil**: **Ben evli değilim**.

L7.title: Questions with mI
not_yet: var mı? 'is there?' → L8
mI with verbs (Geliyor musun?) → L16; after the past (Geldin mi?) → L31
negative questions (Öğrenci değil misin?) → later review

cards.body:
🧑‍🎓 **Öğrenci misin?** "Are you a student?"
**Evet, öğrenciyim.** "Yes, I'm a student."

The question is a little separate word, **mi**, and the "you are" ending rides on it: **mi·sin**.

cards.title: mI: a separate word
cards.body:
Put **mI** right after the word you're asking about. It is written **separately**, but it still follows **4-way harmony** with that word's last vowel:

| Last vowel | mI = | Example |
|---|---|---|
| a ı | **mı** | Hasta **mı**? |
| e i | **mi** | Öğretmen **mi**? |
| o u | **mu** | Doktor **mu**? |
| ö ü | **mü** | Türk **mü**? |

The **m** never changes. In the 3rd person, that's all: *Ayşe öğretmen mi?* "Is Ayşe a teacher?"

cards.title: The person ending goes on mI
cards.body:
| | hasta | öğrenci |
|---|---|---|
| ben | hasta **mıyım**? | öğrenci **miyim**? |
| sen | hasta **mısın**? | öğrenci **misin**? |
| o | hasta **mı**? | öğrenci **mi**? |
| biz | hasta **mıyız**? | öğrenci **miyiz**? |
| siz | hasta **mısınız**? | öğrenci **misiniz**? |
| onlar | hasta**lar mı**? | öğrenci**ler mi**? |

- mI ends in a vowel, so *-(y)Im / -(y)Iz* take the **y**: mı·**y**ım, mi·**y**iz.
- **They:** -lAr stays on the word: *Öğrenciler mi?* (not ~~öğrenci miler~~).

cards.title: Stress and intonation
cards.body:
🔊 The stress jumps to the syllable **just before mI**, and the voice rises there: *has**TA** mı?* · *öğren**Cİ** misin?* · ***TÜRK** müsün?*

mI itself is never stressed.

cards.title: Question words: no mI
cards.body:
| | |
|---|---|
| **ne** | what | *Bu ne?* |
| **kim** | who | *O kim?* |
| **nerede** | where | *Ali nerede?* |
| **nasıl** | how | *Nasılsın?* |

A question word already makes the question, so **never** add mI: *Ali nerede?* (not ~~Ali nerede mi?~~).

With a question word, the person ending goes on the question word: **Nasılsın?** "How are you?" — **İyiyim.** "I'm fine." (Polite: *Nasılsınız?*)

feedback.hasta misin: **mI** follows the last vowel of **hasta**: **a** → **mı**: **hasta mısın**.
feedback.hasta mı sın: The person ending is attached to **mI**: **hasta mısın**.

feedback.yorgunmusun: **mI** is written as a **separate word**: **yorgun musun**.
feedback.yorgun mısın: Look at the last vowel of **yorgun**, **u**: o u → **mu**: **yorgun musun**.

feedback.Türkmüsün: **mI** is written as a **separate word**: **Türk müsün**.

feedback.öğrenci miler: In the 3rd person plural, **-lAr** stays on the word: **öğrenciler mi**.

feedback.hasta mıım: **mI** ends in a vowel, so -(y)Im needs the buffer **y**: **hasta mıyım**.

L8.title: var / yok
not_yet: where something is (Evde kedi var) → L10
having (Arabam var) → L23
past (vardı / yoktu) → L32

cards.body:
☕ **Çay var mı?** "Is there any tea?"
**Var.** "There is." · **Yok.** "There isn't."

Two little words do a lot of work in a Turkish café.

cards.title: var and yok
cards.body:
**var** = there is / there are · **yok** = there isn't / there aren't. They go at the **end**:

| | |
|---|---|
| Kahve **var**. | There's coffee. |
| Süt **yok**. | There's no milk. |
| Çay **yok**, kahve **var**. | There's no tea, there's coffee. |

After *çok* the noun stays singular (L4): *Çok ekmek var.* "There's a lot of bread."

cards.title: Asking and answering
cards.body:
Ask with **mı** (L7): ***var mı?*** · ***yok mu?***

*Ekmek var mı?* "Is there any bread?" — **Var.** / **Yok.**

✅ Answer with **var** or **yok**. A bare *Evet* or *Hayır* sounds unfinished; *Evet, var.* and *Hayır, yok.* are fine.

🔊 The voice rises on **var**: *Çay **VAR** mı?*

cards.title: yok or değil?
cards.body:
Both mean "not", but they answer different questions:

| | |
|---|---|
| **yok**: it isn't **there** | *Peynir yok.* "There's no cheese." |
| **değil**: it isn't **that** (L6) | *Bu peynir değil.* "This isn't cheese." |

items.translation: There's coffee.
There's no milk.

items.note: Kahve var mı? asks if there is coffee; Bu kahve mi? asks if this is coffee.

For 'there isn't', use **yok**, not değil: **Hayır, yok.**

feedback.mi: **mI** follows the last vowel of **var** (a) → **mı**: **var mı**.

items.translation: There's no cheese.

items.note: yok = not there; değil = not that.

L9.title: Adjectives & numbers 1–10
not_yet: numbers 11–1000, kaç, prices → L25
comparison (daha büyük, en güzel) → L29
adjectives with -lI / -sIz (şekerli) → L28

cards.body:
🏡 **Güzel bir ev.** "A beautiful house."
**Ev çok güzel.** "The house is very beautiful."

Same words, different order, different meaning.

cards.title: Adjective first, bir in the middle
cards.body:
As in English, the adjective comes **before** the noun. But **bir** sits **between** them:

| Turkish | English |
|---|---|
| büyük ev | (the) big house |
| büyük **bir** ev | **a** big house |
| kırmızı **bir** araba | **a** red car |

❌ ~~bir büyük ev~~ (that word order means something else; don't use it yet)

cards.title: The house is big
cards.body:
To say what something **is like**, put the adjective **after** the noun, with no "is" (L3):

| describing | saying |
|---|---|
| büyük bir ev "a big house" | Ev büyük. "The house is big." |
| kırmızı bir araba "a red car" | Araba kırmızı. "The car is red." |

**çok** before an adjective = **very**: *Ev çok güzel.* · *çok güzel bir ev* "a very beautiful house".

cards.title: Numbers 1–10
cards.body:
| | | | | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 **bir** | 2 **iki** | 3 **üç** | 4 **dört** | 5 **beş** |
| 6 **altı** | 7 **yedi** | 8 **sekiz** | 9 **dokuz** | 10 **on** |

After a number the noun stays **singular** (L4): *üç kedi* "three cats", *beş kitap var* "there are five books".

Number, then adjective, then noun: *dört büyük ev* "four big houses".

feedback.bir güzel ev: **bir** goes between the adjective and the noun: **güzel bir ev**.

feedback.kitaplar: After a number, the noun stays singular: **üç kitap**.

w.nerede.notes: Contains the locative: nere·de. Explained in L10.

w.değil.notes: Takes the personal endings: değilim, değilsin…

w.nereden.notes: nere·den: the ablative of nere-. Neredensin? 'Where are you from?'

w.de.notes: Clitic, written separately: de after e i ö ü, da after a ı o u. Never te/ta.

w.pazar.notes: Also 'Sunday' (T17). Replaces okul in T9.p1: okul is an L2 core word.

w.keçi.notes: Moved up from T10 pack 3 to replace kedi, which is an L2 core word.

w.Paris.notes: Pronounced as spelled, so harmony is regular: Paris'te, Paris'ten.

w.gitmek.notes: t → d before a vowel: gidin, gidiyor.

w.yemek.notes: ye → yi: yiyin, yiyor. Also the noun 'food, meal'.

w.bakmak.notes: Takes the dative: Kediye bak! 'Look at the cat!' (L17). No k → ğ: bakın, bakıyor.

w.etmek.notes: Mostly in pairs: teşekkür etmek, dans etmek. t → d before a vowel.

w.demek.notes: Bu ne demek? 'What does this mean?' (T1b).

w.atmak.notes: No t → d: atıyor (only gitmek and etmek change).

w.bisiklet.notes: Final t usually stays: bisiklete, bisikleti.

w.bilet.notes: Final t usually stays: bilete, bileti.

w.binmek.notes: Takes the dative: otobüse binmek 'to get on the bus'.

w.korkmak.notes: Takes the ablative: köpekten korkmak 'to be afraid of dogs'.

w.hoşlanmak.notes: Takes the ablative: çaydan hoşlanmak 'to like tea'.

w.saç.notes: One syllable: no softening (saça, saçı). T18 word.

w.kurt.notes: One-syllable exception: softens (kurda, kurdu). T10 pack 2 word.

w.Zonguldak.notes: Names never soften in writing: Zonguldak'a (said with ğ).

w.portakal.notes: Polysyllabic but ends in l: no change (portakala).

w.sevmek.notes: Takes the accusative for a specific object: Ayşe'yi seviyorum.

w.abla.notes: Also a friendly way to address a young woman.

w.ağabey.notes: Usually pronounced, and often written, abi.

w.amca.notes: Also a polite way to address an older man.

w.teyze.notes: Also a polite way to address an older woman.

w.lütfen.notes: T1 pack 2 word; used for real from L14.

w.Türkçe.notes: T4 language. Not a name: no apostrophe (Türkçede).

w.şu.notes: L3. Nearer than o, or pointing at something both speakers can see. Takes n before case endings: şunu, şuna.

w.ad.notes: One syllable: no softening (adım, adın, adı). Adın ne? 'What's your name?'

w.mama.notes: kedi maması 'cat food', köpek maması 'dog food'.

w.kaç.notes: Followed by a singular noun: Kaç kardeşin var? Prices ('Kaç lira?') in L25.

w.ağrımak.notes: Başım ağrıyor. 'My head hurts.' The body part takes the possessive.

w.geçmiş_olsun.notes: Said to anyone who is ill or has had bad luck.

w.ayakkabı.notes: Historically a compound, now an ordinary word: ayakkabılar, ayakkabım.

w.lira.notes: Turkish lira. 'Kaç lira?' 'How many lira?' in L25.

w.Türk.notes: T4 nationality. Capitalised, but no apostrophe before endings: Türküm.

w.buçuk.notes: Saat üç buçuk 'half past three'. 12:30: on iki buçuk or yarım.

w.ne_zaman.notes: Question word: Ne zaman geldin? 'When did you come?'

w.pazartesi.notes: Days are lowercase. pazar + ertesi 'the day after Sunday'.

w.ile.notes: Separate word, never changes. Suffix form -(y)lA: otobüsle, arabayla.

w.nereli.notes: nere·li: Nerelisin? 'Where are you from?' (phrase in L5, explained in L28).

w.daha.notes: Optional after X-DAn: At köpekten (daha) büyük.

w.merhaba.notes: Stressed on the first syllable: MERhaba.

w.kız.notes: Minimal pairs (L1): kız / kaz, kır / kir.

w.cam.notes: The material. A drinking glass is bardak.

w.dağ.notes: ğ lengthens the vowel: 'daa'. Also on the T21 list.

w.çok.notes: çok + singular noun: çok kitap 'a lot of books' (L4). çok + adjective: çok güzel 'very beautiful' (L9).

w.eski.notes: For things (eski bir ev). Old people: yaşlı (later).

w.nasıl.notes: Nasılsın? 'How are you?' Question words never take mI.

w.geçen.notes: geçen hafta 'last week', geçen yıl 'last year'. Literally 'passing' (geçmek).

w.gelecek.notes: gelecek hafta 'next week'. The future form of gelmek used as an adjective: 'the coming week'.

w.yardım.notes: yardım etmek 'to help' (+ dative): Sana yardım edeceğim.

w.istemek.notes: Regular: istiyorum, istedim, isteyeceğim. + -mAk 'want to': Gitmek istiyorum.

w.lazım.notes: Never changes: Gitmem lazım 'I need to go', Bana su lazım 'I need water'.

w.gerekmek.notes: Mostly the negative: Gitmen gerekmiyor 'you don't need to go'.

w.yağmak.notes: Yağmur yağıyor 'it's raining', Kar yağdı 'it snowed'.

w.tatil.notes: tatile gitmek 'to go on holiday', tatilde 'on holiday'.

w.hoşça_kal.notes: Said by the one leaving. Polite / plural: hoşça kalın.

w.efendim.notes: Also how many people answer the phone.

w.kolay_gelsin.notes: Said to someone who is working (culture card).

w.kahvaltı.notes: Historically a compound, now an ordinary word: kahvaltıda.
